Recyclable Poly(urethane-urea) Covalent Adaptable Network Foams via Catalyst-, Isocyanate-, and Additive-Free Synthesis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract For decades, poly(urethane-urea) (PUU) foam production has relied on hazardous isocyanates and a complex array of external catalysts and blowing agents, resulting in chemically persistent materials that defy recycling. Herein, we break this convention by reporting the first-ever synthesis of high-performance PUU foams through an entirely autonomous, isocyanate-free, and additive-free pathway. By leveraging the ring-opening of thiazolidin-2-one with multifunctional amines, we establish a streamlined reaction that simultaneously constructs a covalent adaptable network (CAN) and triggers in situ CO2 evolution. This chemistry bypasses traditional reagents; instead, internal thiol groups react with ethylene carbonate to drive foaming under entirely catalyst-free conditions. By precisely tuning the tris(2-aminoethyl)amine ratio, we synchronize gas expansion with matrix vitrification, overcoming the structural collapse typical of nontraditional systems. The resulting foams feature hindered urea linkages that impart dissociative CAN behavior, enabling full chemical reprocessability and structural recovery over multiple cycles without compromising mechanical integrity. With an open-cell architecture and acoustic performance comparable to those of the tested commercial reference materials under the present measurement conditions, this work provides a promising strategy for designing circular cellular materials that contribute to a zero-waste chemical economy.

title: Manganese-Doped Fluorinated Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-90 for Activatable 1H/19F MRI and Metalloimmunotherapy of Hepatocellular Carcinoma
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In the immunotherapy of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is substantially limited by the complex and highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Therefore, developing approaches to effectively reverse the immunosuppressive TME while enabling accurate HCC imaging poses a major unmet challenge. To tackle this critical challenge, we rationally designed and constructed a hyaluronic acid (HA)-functionalized manganese-doped fluorinated zeolitic imidazolate framework-90 (ZIF-90) nanosystem (ZM-F6@HA NPs) for integrated theranostic applications in HCC. This nanosystem not only enabled noninvasive and precise visualization of HCC lesions through GSH-activatable 1H/19F MRI for diagnostic purposes, but also induced robust tumor-associated inflammation and promoted potent antitumor adaptive immunity through synergistic mechanisms, including cGAS–STING pathway activation, immunogenic cell death (ICD) induction, and pyroptosis induction in HCC cells. The activated antitumor immune response effectively remodeled the immunosuppressive TME, and its combination with ICIs results in significant tumor regression and substantial inhibition of lung metastasis. This responsive ZIF-90-based multifunctional nanosystem provides a promising and rational strategy for integrated diagnosis and combinatorial immunotherapy of HCC.

title: Hydrophilic Hairy Dual Signal-Responsive Ratiometric Fluorescent Molecularly Imprinted Polymer Microspheres for Smartphone-Assisted Visual Herbicide Detection in the Undiluted Milks
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The efficient development of high-performance complex biological sample-compatible fluorescent molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) and their portable sensors is highly important for their real-world applications but remains challenging. Herein, we report on the efficient synthesis of hydrophilic hairy dual signal-responsive ratiometric fluorescent MIP microspheres and their smartphone-assisted highly sensitive and precise visual detection of 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) in the undiluted pure milks. Core-shell-corona-structured 2,4-D-MIP particles with both green and red fluorescent species-labeling and polyethylene glycol brushes were readily synthesized via the newly developed one-pot surface-initiated activator-regenerated by electron transfer atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP) with tris[2-(dimethylamino)ethyl]amine as both the ligand and the reducing agent for Cu(II) catalyst. This synthetic strategy could not only afford largely enhanced polymerization rate but also lead to fluorescent 2,4-D-MIP particles with obviously enhanced fluorescence responses toward 2,4-D compared with those prepared via the previously developed one-pot surface-initiated ATRP methods. Such hydrophilic dual fluorescent 2,4-D-MIP showed remarkable photostability, reusability, and long-term storage stability as well as strong 2,4-D selectivity and simultaneous large green fluorescence enhancement and red fluorescence quenching toward 2,4-D in pure milk samples, which make them promising complex biological sample-compatible chemosensors for visually detecting 2,4-D with good recoveries (98.0–104.0%) and high accuracy (≤4.0%). Notably, their obvious dual-signal responsivity imparted them with significantly enhanced optosensing sensitivity, with their limit of detection (=0.025 μM) being almost five times lower than that of our previously reported hydrophilic hairy single signal-responsive ratiometric fluorescent 2,4-D-MIPs. Finally, a smartphone-integrated portable MIP optosensor was developed for precise and selective visual 2,4-D detection in pure milks. This study opens new access for efficient development of high-performance MIP optosensors highly promising in on-site detection of complex biological samples.

title: Directed Evolution of a Protein Catenane Reveals How Noncanonical Topology Modulates Sequence–Property Relationships
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Single-domain protein catenanes, in which two mechanically interlocked polypeptide rings fold into a compact structure, provide a tractable system for probing how chemical topology reshapes protein fitness. Using single-domain catenated dihydrofolate reductase (cat-DHFR) as a model, we combined homologue expansion, directed evolution, and topology reversion to compare matched linear and catenated isoforms. Catenation proved broadly compatible with DHFR homologues, yet soluble yield and catalytic activity remained strongly sequence dependent. Directed evolution substantially improved the catalytic activity of cat-DHFR through enhanced substrate binding and turnover, while largely preserving or increasing thermal stability. Strikingly, reverting evolved catenanes to their linear counterparts transferred these functional gains: all reverted linear isoforms exhibited higher catalytic activity and thermal stability than wild-type DHFR. Across matched topological pairs, catenation generally increased thermal stability, whereas catalytic activity depended more strongly on sequence background and topology. These results demonstrate that chemical topology can modulate the phenotypic effects of sequence variation, while permitting substantial transferability of beneficial mutations across topological contexts. Protein catenanes may therefore serve not only as alternative topological isoforms, but also as evolutionary intermediates en route to linear proteins with simultaneously improved stability and activity.

title: Observation of Orbital-Resolved Conductance in a Single-Molecule Metal–Metal Interaction Channel
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The exploration of unique metallophilic interactions, a pivotal category of intermolecular interactions that govern material properties and reactivity, is crucial for deciphering the role of metal atomic orbitals in their formation and uncovering their fundamental characteristics. However, due to their inherently subtle and delicate nature, these interactions remain exceptionally challenging to detect and characterize. Here, we present a method of utilizing metallophilic interactions to build stable graphene–molecule–graphene single-molecule junctions through molecular engineering. Real-time electrical measurements reveal that the metal atomic orbital contributions in various metal–metal interactions originate from the hybridization of different angular components of intermetallic d and s orbitals (dz2–s/dxy–s), a conclusion further corroborated by theoretical calculations. Distinct overlaps between intermetallic orbitals give rise to diverse molecular configurations, leading to corresponding orbital-resolved conductance. Furthermore, we establish the relationship between the orbital interaction and experimental transition activation energy through counterion- and metal-dependent measurements. This work uncovers the underlying mechanism of metal–metal interactions, bridges the gap between covalent bonds and weak interactions, and extends the research scope of molecular electronics.

title: Mechanistic Study of CO2 Reduction in a Metal Nanoparticle/Ligand-Based Nanoconfined Pocket
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochemically reducing CO2 holds promise for producing value-added chemicals. Achieving this requires electrocatalysts with high selectivity and energy efficiency. Nanopocket engineering enhances catalytic activity by modulating interfacial reactivity and stabilizing key intermediates, especially those involved in the rate-determining step. Here, we use density functional theory to systematically evaluate the CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) and the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) on three systems: Ag surface without confinement, double Ag confinement, and Ag surface confined by a ligand in the absence and presence of interfacial water. We find that decreasing the confinement distance from 7 to 4 Å stabilizes CO2RR intermediates over HER in the double Ag and Ag/ligand systems, due to additional secondary interactions, such as hydrogen bonding, in the latter. The hydrogen bonding network is further enhanced in the presence of interfacial water, resulting in increased *COOH stabilization over *H in Ag/ligand and double Ag systems at a 7 Å confinement distance. The increased stabilization of *COOH over *H can be attributed to the high selectivity and activity for CO2RR in Ag/ligand catalysts. These results systematically reveal how nanoconfinement can be an effective strategy for controlling reactivity at the gas–liquid–solid interfaces toward highly selective CO2RR.

title: Keep AI-augmented science contestable
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving upstream in science. Systems such as AlphaFold have already transformed protein-structure prediction, while newer agentic systems can search literatures, generate hypotheses, write and execute code, interpret results, and automate much of the path from idea to paper. Recent debates have asked how such systems may change scientific progress, surprise, and human understanding. Yet they also change something more fundamental: who—or what—participates in deciding which questions are asked, which evidence is surfaced, and which alternatives survive. As machine intelligence becomes part of science’s epistemic infrastructure, steps must be taken to ensure that researchers who did not build, own, or operate the system can still contest how ideas and evidence became a claim.

title: Bio-inspired self-assembly of ordered interface topology for robust composite solid electrolytes
abstract: A bio-inspired self-assembly strategy enables composite solid-state electrolytes with fast ion transport, stable interfaces, strong dendrite suppression, high conductivity, mechanical robustness, and excellent cycling stability.

title: Designing for effective heat transfer in a solid thermal energy storage system
abstract: Thermal energy storage using solid sensible heating is a potential low-cost technology for long-duration energy storage. Channels for the heat transfer fluid are often embedded within the storage blocks for heating (charging) and cooling (discharging). Here, we present design principles to improve channel-embedded thermal storage performance and apply them to a system featuring graphite and liquid tin. First, we analyze the impact of geometry and material properties, determining ideal channel spacing and block connectivity (series vs. parallel) to achieve high (dis)charge temperature uniformity. Next, we determine how controlling fluid flow rate, heating infrastructure, and heat engine operation can enhance discharge power uniformity and accelerate charging. Finally, we implement these principles on a 100-block, 200 MWh thermal storage system, demonstrating significant improvement for both discharging (constant discharge power for 90% of rated duration) and charging ( 90% charged within 4 h). Overall, this hierarchical design procedure enables low-cost, high-performing solid sensible thermal energy storage.

title: Ligand‐Directed Molecular Beacons as Turn‐On Fluorescent Probes for Sensing Cell‐Surface Receptor‐Ligand Interactions
abstract: ABSTRACT Cell‐surface receptors are essential biomarkers and therapeutic targets, yet detecting them in native biological environments remains challenging. Turn‐on, ligand‐directed fluorescent probes have advanced the study of these receptors by enabling low‐background imaging and the sensing of interactions with binding partners. However, their broader utility is hindered by the difficulty of tuning specificity, binding affinity, and emission properties for each new target. Here, we introduce a highly modular molecular beacon (MB)‐based platform that overcomes these limitations. Building on the spatial proximity of many cell‐surface receptors and the conformational switching of MBs, we designed multivalent, ligand‐appended hairpin probes that strongly engage these receptors while undergoing stem opening and fluorescence activation at the cell surface. This design, together with the structural programmability of these single‐stranded DNA constructs, enables tuning of emission wavelength, receptor selectivity, and binding strength through simple exchange of fluorophores and ligands, and modulation of valency. For rapidly endocytosed receptors, we further demonstrate an alternative long‐stem MB design that exploits intracellular probe cleavage to trigger fluorescence. By applying these MBs to image distinct receptors, distinguish cellular states, and detect receptor–inhibitor interactions under wash‐free conditions, we demonstrate a versatile and generalizable strategy for probing cell‐surface receptors in living cells.

title: Redundant Submodule-Based Valve-Side Single-Phase-to-Ground Fault Protection in MMC-MVDC Distribution Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a redundant submodule (SM)-based protection scheme for modular multilevel converter-based medium voltage dc (MMC-MVDC) distribution systems under valve-side single-phase-to-ground (SPG) faults. Both symmetrical monopolar and bipolar MMC station configurations are studied, considering half-bridge SMs (HBSMs), full-bridge SMs (FBSMs), and hybrid SMs for each converter station. Redundant SMs normally operate in bypass state and transition into a blocking state once a valve-side SPG fault is detected. In symmetrical monopolar MMCs, the use of unipolar redundant SMs can prevent upper and lower arm overvoltage following converter blocking. However, bipolar redundant SMs are required in the bipolar MMC to mitigate upper arm overvoltage in systems with HBSMs, FBSMs and hybrid SMs, lower arm overvoltage in systems with hybrid SMs, as well as to address the issue of non-zero crossings of grid-side currents in systems with HBSMs. Simulation results in PSCAD/EMTDC validate the effectiveness of the proposed redundant SM-based protection methods for MMC-MVDC distribution systems under valve-side SPG faults.

title: Mathematical Framework for Harmonic Analysis of Cluster Stream Buffer Switching in MMC HVDC: Chebyshev-Based Approach and Insulation
abstract: This paper presents a novel analytical framework for harmonic characterization of the Cluster Stream Buffer (CSB) switching method in Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC)-based Voltage Source Converters (VSCs). Due to the nonlinear nature of Nearest Level Control (NLC), conventional Fourier-based approaches are not well suited for harmonic analysis of CSB. To address this limitation, a Chebyshev polynomial-based method is proposed, enabling a closed-form representation of harmonic components as functions of the modulation index and switching level. The proposed approach provides improved analytical insight and computational efficiency compared to conventional methods. Furthermore, a design methodology integrating harmonic analysis with dielectric stress evaluation is introduced for optimal switching level selection. The results show that a minimum of 33 levels is required under typical conditions, while higher levels (e.g., 49 levels) may be necessary under increased harmonic stress.

title: Coordinated Control and Protection Strategy for Transmission Lines Connected to Grid-Forming Inverter-Based Resources
abstract: Compared to traditional grid-following (GFL) control, grid-forming (GFM) inverters possess the capability to actively support the grid; however, they retain the inherent characteristics of limited fault current amplitude and controlled phase. To address the degraded adaptability of distance protection on outgoing transmission lines integrated with GFM inverters, this paper proposes a coordinated strategy between GFM control and distance protection. First, based on the compound sequence network, the analytical relationship between the additional reactance component and the fault current phase is analyzed. Consequently, ideal fault current phases required to eliminate measurement errors are derived. Second, an adaptive virtual impedance control-protection coordination strategy based on sequence component separation is proposed. The positive-sequence control loop regulates parameters to track the ideal phase and eliminate the measured reactance error, while the negative-sequence loop suppresses voltage unbalance and provides voltage support. PSCAD/EMTDC simulations demonstrate that, without modifying existing protection configurations or requiring remote communication, the proposed strategy effectively eliminates the impact of the additional reactance. Consequently, it ensures the reliable operation of distance protection and maintains excellent adaptability and reliability in multi-IBR scenarios.

title: Supervisory Control Framework for a Hybrid PV-BESS Inverter Under Power Export Constraint
abstract: This paper presents a practical supervisory energy management framework for a hybrid photovoltaic (PV)-battery energy storage system (BESS) inverter operating under a grid export constraint. The strategy reconciles two conflicting objectives: to maximize PV energy utilization and to minimize BESS cycling energy while requiring almost no inverter firmware modification. Unlike conventional inverter-embedded methods with limited control flexibility, the proposed framework introduces a vendor-independent supervisory controller that interfaces with a hybrid inverter through standard Modbus/RS-485 communication. A compact five-mode control architecture enables rapid adaptation to load variations, improved PV operating point selection, and coordinated BESS dispatch with minimal cycling stress. Experimental validation across eight representative scenarios spanning seasonal irradiance variability and weekday/weekend load patterns demonstrates significant performance gains. During summer, spring, and autumn, grid import decreases by 93%, the self-sufficiency ratio increases from 45.7–65.5% to 74.6–78.9%, and PV curtailment decreases consistently. Furthermore, the annual grid expenditure is reduced by nearly 80%. Economic analysis indicates favorable viability, with a payback period of 1.9 years when accounting for grid savings and conservative BESS lifetime extension benefits. The proposed supervisory energy management system achieves superior PV utilization, enhanced operational autonomy, and substantial economic benefits, offering a scalable, retrofit-compatible solution for export-constrained residential and commercial PV-BESS installations.

title: An Adaptive Graph Convolution-Based Bi-Level Planning Strategy for Urban Fast-Charging Stations in Electricity-Transportation Coupled Networks
abstract: To address the mismatch between massive charging requirement triggers and limited charging resource supply in Electricity-Transportation Coupled Networks (ETCNs), this paper proposes a bi-level planning strategy for urban fast-charging stations (FCSs). First, given the topological interdependence and feature interactions of ETCNs, a unified graph-structured representation model is constructed to characterize the dynamic transmission of energy and information among multiple agents in “vehicles-stations-networks”. Second, adaptive graph convolution is designed in the upper layer. Through multi-order neighborhood aggregation and adaptive weights, the inherent physical-electrical correlation knowledge among multiple agents is learned, enabling multi-dimensional feature extraction of ETCNs and differentiated weight allocation to transportation nodes. The physical constraints of ETCN operation are embedded in the feature loss as regularization, thereby constructing a semi-supervised learning paradigm driven by data-feature collaboration loss. Then, based on the candidate FCS set initially screened by the upper layer, an equilibrium evaluation index is established to suppress node congestion and service blind areas. In the lower layer, a multi-objective optimization model is constructed to jointly solve the connection location of FCSs in the electricity network and the capacity configuration of charging piles. Finally, case studies are conducted within a practical functional zone in Hong Kong, China. Experimental results verify the superiority of the proposed method under different planning scenarios.

title: Optimal Operation Trajectory Control of Variable Speed Pumped Storage for Power System Frequency Regulation
abstract: Variable speed pumped storage (VSPS) possesses significant potential for power system frequency regulation. This paper proposes a novel optimal trajectory control for VSPS to enhance power system frequency response (FR) by fully leveraging its regulation potential, while maintaining its rotor speed stability. First, the speed stability of VSPS during FR process in both turbine and pump modes is investigated. Following this, an analytical expression for the rotor speed is derived, specifically for the turbine mode, given its susceptibility to speed instability. This expression enables not only an efficient assessment of rotor overspeed risks but also a precise characterization of critical points along the operational trajectory. Then, the design principles of additional power control for VSPS are proposed to achieve a smooth switch of operation stages. Based on these principles and derived expressions, the optimal operation trajectory of VSPS is determined by system disturbances and the unit’s operating conditions. This adaptability of the proposed strategy optimizes power response and strengthens FR capability. Furthermore, an overspeed control is developed to ensure rotor speed stability. Finally, the IEEE 39-bus system is utilized to test the proposed strategy under various operating conditions, demonstrating its superior performance in improving power system FR.

title: Wind Farm Cooperative Yaw Predictive Control Against Model Uncertainty via Continuous Learning From SCADA Data
abstract: Cooperative yaw control is a critical solution to reduce wake effect and improve power generation of wind farms, and its implementation based on analytical wake model is crucial to realizing its engineering practice. However, the inherent model uncertainty raises challenges. To this end, this paper proposes an application-oriented framework that allows SCADA data to engage cooperative yaw control, which can improve model adaptability and ensure power gain. First, considering the operation principle of industrial yaw system, a novel cooperative yaw predictive control with yaw rate as control action is introduced. Importantly, a continuous learning strategy against model uncertainty is proposed, which is composed of three mechanisms: outlier online detection using model prior knowledge, working scenario generation by distance dependent Chinese restaurant processes, and parameter learning with Bayesian inference. Finally, the result derived from Penmanshiel wind farm demonstrates that the proposed strategy can assimilate SCADA data well with a promising potential for engineering application of model-based cooperative yaw control.

title: Flexibilizing Grid-Connected Renewable Power to Ammonia Systems via a Novel Hydrogen Storage Design: Configuration and Operational Strategy
abstract: Renewable power to ammonia (ReP2A) offers a promising route for renewable energy utilization. To fully utilize volatile renewable generation without breaking process continuity, ReP2A systems require hydrogen storage subsystems with storage tanks and compressors. However, the conventional layout of hydrogen storage subsystems can cause significant hydrogen supply pressure variations, restricting the ReP2A system to a semi-steady-state operation inadequate for handling renewable fluctuations. In practice, feedforward control based on short-term forecasts is widely employed, yet forecast errors necessitate substantial grid electricity purchases to maintain continuity. This coupling between power and chemical manufacturing increases grid peak-shaving pressure and undermines economic benefits. To address these challenges, a novel hydrogen storage subsystem with a parallel-connected compressor is proposed to enhance pressure regulation, alongside a capacity allocation method and a state-transition-based PID (ST-PID) control strategy. Furthermore, a multi-timescale framework embeds the ST-PID controller to bridge real-time control and long-term optimization. Case studies with real-world data demonstrate that the proposed system unlocks the flexibility for renewable consumption and shows robustness against prediction errors, reducing grid electricity reliance by 38.56% and lowering the levelized cost of ammonia by 8.75%. This offers dual benefits in promoting renewable integration and enhancing economic performance.

title: Coordinated Planning Strategy for Airborne Wind Energy in Ground-Based Power Grids
abstract: High-altitude wind energy offers a promising renewable resource, particularly for inland regions with limited surface wind. Airborne Wind Energy Systems (AWESs) capture and convert high-altitude wind into electricity, offering a novel approach to diversify and decarbonize the energy supply. Unlike conventional wind systems, AWESs can dynamically adjust their operating height to maximize energy capture, but this capability introduces a large decision space that complicates their integration into multi-source power systems. To address this challenge, we propose a long-term planning and operational optimization framework for AWESs within multi-source power systems. First, a two-stage stochastic programming model is developed to incorporate AWES into uncertain operating scenarios, while a mixed-integer linear formulation defines its maximum power output potential to narrow the altitude-related decision space in operation phase. Second, to mitigate computational complexity, a problem-driven scenario reduction strategy based on the PCCK-Medoids algorithm is applied. Finally, case studies across five western Chinese provinces demonstrate that AWESs integration enhances clean energy complementarity and system performance: renewable penetration increases by up to 23 percentage points, storage requirements decline by 65%, and annualized costs fall by 14%. These findings highlight the potential of AWESs to reduce reliance on high-cost resources and support power system decarbonization.

title: Low-Carbon Scheduling for Power-Hydrogen Integrated Energy System Using Large Language Model Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Power-hydrogen integrated energy systems (PH-IESs) are emerging as a promising solution to achieve net-zero carbon emissions. However, the large-scale integration of uncertain renewable energy sources (RESs) and flexible demand-side resources (e.g., hydrogen electrolysis) pose great challenges in the real-time low-carbon scheduling of PH-IESs. This paper proposes a novel source-demand coordinated low-carbon scheduling framework for PH-IESs, empowered by deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and large language model (LLM) techniques. The proposed framework systematically integrates source-side generation with demand-side flexible hydrogen loads to improve carbon reduction and economic efficiency. An LLM-enhanced carbon flow pattern recognition and inference mechanism is developed to enable accurate predictions of real-time carbon intensity under complex, high-dimensional operating conditions. An LLM-enhanced DRL algorithm is then proposed to directly generate optimal scheduling strategies for the flexible demand-side resources, which can overcome computational bottlenecks in real-time decision-making. Numerical simulations on two PH-IESs are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating DRL and LLM techniques for intelligent, efficient, and low-carbon operation of PH-IESs.

title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Virtual Inertia Pinning Control for Heterogeneous VSGs
Multi-Mode Response Mechanism and Fault Ride-Through Control for Renewable Energy Integrated System via Grid-Forming VSC-HVDC
abstract: The renewable energy integrated system via grid-forming voltage source converter-based high voltage direct current (VSC-HVDC) has become a critical pathway for modern power systems. Existing studies have not adequately considered the impact of abrupt variations in the equivalent grid impedance under symmetrical faults on the power angle response, or the control interaction between the virtual synchronous generator-based grid-end converter (VSG-GEC) and the renewable energy-end converter (REEC), which may lead to power angle instability of VSG-GEC or cause severe disturbances to the renewable energy island. This paper analyzes the power-angle characteristics of VSG-GEC and reveals a multi-mode response mechanism resulting from the interaction between the outer-loop controller of VSG-GEC and the faulted grid with equivalent impedance variation. The constraints on the control reference values of VSG-GEC are derived to prevent power angle instability and avoid AC overcurrent, thereby establishing a fault ride-through feasible region considering multi-mode responses. A fault ride-through control method based on response mode adjustment is then developed. Validation results demonstrate that the proposed method maintains uninterrupted operation of the grid-forming integrated system while maximizing the active power of VSG-GEC to reduce the REEC control adjustment required to avoid DC overvoltage, thereby mitigating disturbances to the renewable energy island.

title: Reconfiguration-Driven Flexibility Extensions in Coupled Power-Transportation Networks With Uncertainties
abstract: Under high photovoltaic (PV) penetration, distribution networks (DNs) face insufficient operational flexibility across spatial and temporal dimensions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a reconfiguration-driven framework aimed at flexibility extensions for coupled power-transportation networks under uncertainty, to enhance DNs operational flexibility. To framework leverages multi-reconfiguration-driven spatiotemporal controllable devices to enable multi-level reconfiguration of feeders, voltage source converters and modular transportable energy storage systems, thereby facilitating cross-node and cross-period energy coordination while enhancing scheduling flexibility and PV utilization efficiency. To handle uncertainties arising from traffic congestion, load fluctuations, and PV generation, a dynamic distance-based spatiotemporal decision-making method integrated with rolling optimization is developed to represent the time-varying spatial relationships of vehicles and battery modules during transportation and scheduling, while addressing future uncertainties and enhancing the adaptability of the scheduling strategy. Furthermore, modular battery availability screening and safety assurance model are incorporated to support dynamic identification and management of battery modules, preventing over-charging/over-discharging and state mismatches. Simulation studies on both a modified IEEE 33-node distribution network with a 14-node transportation network and a 10 kV, 220-node distribution network in a specific region of Anhui Province, China demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively extends DN flexibility, enhances PV utilization, and ensures reliable operation.

title: Mitigating Power Fluctuations of Large Language Model Training via Hybrid Energy Storage Systems in Renewable-Powered Computing Centers
abstract: As the demand for computing power surges, renewable-powered computing centers (RPCCs) are being deployed at an accelerating pace. During large language model (LLM) training, RPCCs exhibit highly fluctuating, broadband load characteristics that can excite grid resonances and thereby pose significant threats to the secure and stable operation of emerging power systems. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a hybrid energy storage system (HESS) planning approach tailored to mitigate the power fluctuations of RPCCs. First, a signal decomposition method based on symplectic geometric mode decomposition (SGMD) is developed to capture multi-timescale load power fluctuations, on top of which a HESS power allocation strategy is designed. Then, by explicitly accounting for the power fluctuation characteristics of LLM training, an energy storage demand assessment method is established and a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model for HESS planning is formulated. Finally, case studies are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed planning framework and to elucidate the impacts of power fluctuations inherent to different LLM training tasks.

title: A Multi-Mode Sub-Synchronous Damping Controller for Renewable-Thermal-Bundled Power Transmission by LCC-HVDC System
abstract: With the increase of renewable power generation, multiple poorly-damped or unstable sub-synchronous oscillation (SSO) modes induced by various devices may coexist in the renewable-thermal-bundled power transmission by LCC-HVDC system, including SG-based torsional SSOs and converter-based electromagnetic SSOs. Due to the complex dynamic interactions, it is still challenging to develop the consistent interpretation of the control interactive mechanism for different SSO modes, and to design a supplementary controller for multi-mode SSO suppression. To address these, this paper establishes the system equivalent single-input single-output (SISO) transfer function model for each SSO mode, by retaining its dominant energy storage element dynamic of the correlated device, and then their respective SSO stability is evaluated from a unified damping torque perspective. Subsequently, the interaction paths of key control loops contributing to the damping of each SSO mode are derived. On this basis, a damping enhancement capability index is proposed to identify the preferred control loop for the damping controller placement. Based on phase compensation and gain adjustment of the key control loop interaction path, a multi-mode sub-synchronous damping controller (MSDC) is proposed to realize the targeted damping compensation for different modes. Finally, the proposed MSDC approach is validated on a PV-thermal-bundled power transmission by LCC-HVDC system, which effectively suppresses the PV-induced, LCC-induced or SG-induced SSOs.

title: Small-Signal Security Region of Floating Offshore Wind Turbine Under Wind and Wave Disturbances
abstract: The wind and wave disturbances of floating offshore wind turbine (FOWT) present significant challenges for small-signal security analysis, due to the nonlinear aero-hydro dynamics and variable working points. This paper proposes a mechanical-electrical coupling FOWT model and analyzes its stability under wind and wave disturbances, deriving the stable operating area. The model incorporates both the mechanical torque applied to the generator and the electrical torque of the generator affects the mechanical dynamics. Compared with a fixed-bottom wind turbine (FWT), new oscillation modes are revealed for the linearized FOWT model to analyze its stability. Based on the FOWT model, the small-signal security region (SSSR) is formulated, offering a geometric representation of the stability boundaries under wind and wave injection space. Due to the coupling characteristics of FOWTs, new dominant oscillation modes leading to Hopf bifurcation on the SSSR boundary are observed, compared with FWT model. Simulations of the proposed model on the single machine infinite system (SMIB) and the four-area system derive the SSSR boundary under wind and wave disturbances, validating the proposed model and SSSR derivation method.

title: ShadowSense: Edge Optimized Self-Supervised Learning for Dynamic Shadow Mapping of Solar Panels
abstract: We introduce ShadowSense, a self-supervised, edge-deployable framework for dynamic shadow mapping and short-term PV power forecasting. Unlike prior methods that require labor-intensive manual annotations or rely on overly complex physical models, ShadowSense uses transient power dips as weak supervision signals, enabling fully unsupervised learning from synchronized sky imagery and power measurements. The architecture integrates a masked spatiotemporal autoencoder to learn cloud motion dynamics, a differentiable geometric projection module to adapt to diverse panel orientations, and a causal alignment system to maintain temporal correspondence between cloud shadows and power responses. Evaluated over 122,400 observations across 92 days in Kaunas, Lithuania, the system achieved a 32.7% reduction in mean absolute error (MAE) compared to baselines, captured 92.3% of rapid power ramps, and operated with an average inference latency of 66 ms and energy cost of 0.52 J per prediction on a solar-powered NVIDIA Jetson Nano, demonstrating scalable, real-time PV forecasting in resource-constrained environments.

title: Bilevel Optimization for Green Hydrogen-to-Ammonia Synthesis System Considering Complex Dynamic Processes and Uncertainties
abstract: The wind-powered green hydrogen-to-ammonia system offers a promising pathway for utilizing marine renewable energy; however, its economic viability is constrained by the strongly nonlinear dynamics of ammonia synthesis and the inherent stochasticity of wind power generation. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a bilevel scheduling framework. In the upper layer, a reduced-order Trend- and Structure-constrained Physics-Informed Neural Network (TS-PINN) model is developed by embedding trend priors and mechanistic constraints, effectively capturing the nonlinear characteristics of the ammonia synthesis process with significantly reduced computational effort. An improved Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) algorithm is then employed to co-optimize operational strategies and key reactor setpoints, including bed temperature and pressure. In the lower layer, a Wasserstein-distance-based distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model is established to coordinate hydrogen production and storage operations to hedge against wind power uncertainty. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an effective balance among modeling accuracy, economic performance, and operational robustness, while accounting for coupled reaction–heat-transfer dynamics and renewable generation uncertainty.

title: Global Transient Stability Control for Grid-Following Inverter Based on Elimination of Pendulum-like Periodic Trajectory
abstract: From the perspective of pendulum-like system, this letter analyzes the transient instability mechanism of grid-following (GFL) inverter. Based on it, a global transient stability control is proposed, by eliminating the second category periodic trajectory of pendulum-like system. Compared with previous methods, the proposed control can achieve transient stability during extreme and severe weak grid faults.

title: Scheduling for Hybrid Microgrids With Renewable Energy Sources and Hydrogen Storage: Data-Correlated Uncertainty Modeling and Semi-Convex Relaxation
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources (RESs), hydrogen energy storage (HES), and electric vehicles (EVs) is critical to the decarbonization of electric power production; however, it introduces significant challenges for microgrid energy management owing principally to RES uncertainty and the non-convex constraints associated with HES and EV operations. The present work addresses these challenges by applying data-driven uncertainty set optimization and semi-convex relaxation approaches. First, a probability-driven data-correlated uncertainty set is developed using historical data distributions to generate RES uncertainty representations with reduced conservativeness under significantly reduced computational burden. Second, a closed-loop semi-convex relaxation procedure is designed to manage the non-convex operational constraints of HES and EV operations, where the NP-hard nature of these constraints is addressed by iteratively enforcing only violated binary conditions, which ensures solution accuracy with minimal computational overhead. Third, the resulting tri-level robust energy management model is solved efficiently by a customized column-and-constraint generation algorithm incorporating the proposed relaxation procedure. As a result, only those non-convex constraints that are violated in the relaxed solution are included in the energy management solution process. The superiority of the proposed approach over existing state-of-the-art methods in enabling higher penetrations of clean energy technologies is demonstrated through numerical case studies on a practical hybrid microgrid system.

title: A Quantum-Assisted Boltzmann Machine for Wind Power Probabilistic Learning
abstract: Accurate probabilistic modeling of renewable power is essential for the secure operation and control of modern power systems. However, learning and modeling the data structure with high accuracy remains challenging due to the inherent spatial-temporal correlations of renewables. To address this issue, we propose a novel quantum-assisted Gaussian-Bernoulli restricted Boltzmann machine (GBRBM), which is intrinsically suitable for continuous wind power modeling. Furthermore, we tailor its negative phase to be directly solvable by quantum computing, thereby accelerating the learning process. Experiments conducted on real quantum hardware validate the cost-effective performance of the proposed method.

title: Low-Frequency Oscillation Stability Evaluation of Grid-Forming-Converter-Dominated Power Systems
abstract: To address the well-known concern of sub/super-synchronous oscillation issues driven by the interaction among grid-following converters, there is an increasing use of grid-forming (GFM) converters for renewable integration into power grids. However, it has recently been reported that low-frequency oscillation issues occur in a multi-converter system dominated by GFM converters (named as MCS-GFMC). Since the low-frequency oscillation instability mechanism remains unclear, it is challenging to identify this type of oscillation issues in realistic MCS-GFMCs. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a method for quickly identifying the low-frequency oscillation stability issues from the perspective of grid strength. We first analyze the theoretical relationship between grid strength and low-frequency oscillation stability in a single-GFM-converter system by the system’s closed-loop characteristic equation. Then, this analytical relationship is extended to MCS-GFMCs for developing the proposed method. This method is applicable to large-scale MCS-GFMCs, even with “black-boxed” converters. Two test systems are provided to validate the proposed method.

title: An Optimal Offering and Operating Strategy for Wind-Storage Operators Participating in Grid Inertial Response and Frequency Regulation
abstract: The high penetration of renewable energy generation weakens the power system’s inertia support capability, thereby exacerbating the risk of frequency instability. This paper proposes a bi-level optimal offering and operating strategy that enables wind-storage operators to provide inertial response and frequency regulation service in the power grid with high renewable penetration. The upper level takes operational costs as the objective to quantify the time-varying ability of wind-storage operators for virtual inertia and frequency responses, and the energy dispatch and frequency-regulation services of wind-storage operators are optimally coordinated to support power grid operations at the lower level. Then, the differences in inertial response and frequency regulation dynamics between synchronous generators and wind-storage systems are quantitatively characterized by incorporating frequency-response delays. The frequency security constraints that account for the dynamic inertia characteristics of wind-storage systems are established. Finally, the original bi-level optimization problem is reformulated into an equivalent single-level problem using duality theory and KKT conditions, so as to derive an effective cost-reflective mechanism for providing inertia and frequency regulation services. Comparative results demonstrate that the participation of wind-storage systems in frequency regulation markets can significantly enhance the economic efficiency of power system operations.

title: Short-Term Frequency Regulation for Wind Farms via Stochastic Distribution Control and Image-Based Visual Servoing
abstract: Large-scale wind farms (WFs) are increasingly required to participate in short-term frequency regulation (STFR) during frequency events. To enhance the stability, accuracy, responsiveness, and rapidity of the STFR capability while mitigating the fatigue load of wind turbines, a novel model-free STFR strategy is proposed in this paper based on stochastic distribution control (SDC) theory and image-based visual servoing (IBVS) method for WFs with numerous WTs. The histogram of the frequency is used to guide the WF to implement STFR. By comparing current histogram features with target features, the target frequency histogram tracking control is realized. Meanwhile, by minimizing the active power reference fluctuations for each WT, the fatigue load of each WT is reduced. The optimal active power reference is allocated to individual WTs directly without adopting aggregation and dis-aggregation methods. The simulation results show that the proposed control method improves the STFR capability in terms of stability, accuracy, responsiveness, and rapidity.

title: High-Sensitivity Zero-Sequence Pilot Protection for High-Impedance Faults in Low-Resistance Grounded Distribution Networks
abstract: Reliable detection and rapid isolation of single-phase-to-ground faults (SPGFs) in low-resistance grounded systems (LRGSs) are critical for power utilization safety. However, the conventional zero-sequence (ZS) overcurrent protection method exhibits significant limitations in speed and sensitivity under arcing or high-impedance faults (HIFs). This paper presents a dual-criteria-based pilot protection scheme for HIFs in LRGSs using ZS distribution characteristics. The characteristics of the ZS admittance ratio at the fault point for SPGFs are analyzed, whose minimum value is significantly greater than that at unfaulted points under any situation. The ZS admittance ratio at both ends of the fault section further amplifies the above fault features based on the ZS voltages/currents distribution, which serves as the primary criterion for protection design when protective relays at both terminals are activated. The auxiliary protection logic, a supplementary criterion under HIFs or terminal faults, is triggered by a rise in the single-ended ZS impedance during internal faults. The MATLAB/Simulink simulation and the real-time digital simulator (RTDS) hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves a fault resistance tolerance of 4 kΩ within one power-frequency cycle. Moreover, it maintains reliable performance under challenging conditions, including arcing faults and the integration of distributed generators.

title: Virtual Inertia Limit Estimation Method for Power Systems With High Proportion of Renewable Energy Considering Time Delay
abstract: As the increasing capacity of renewable energy sources (RESs), power system with high RES penetration urgently need virtual inertia support from RESs. Current research has found that, due to inherent time delay, providing excessive virtual inertia from RESs may instead cause small-signal instability in the power system. Therefore, determining the upper limit of virtual inertia from RESs is critical to ensuring small-signal stability. However, current studies have only proposed methods for determining small-signal stability in power systems that consider virtual inertia control (VIC) time delay, with limited discussion of the upper limit of virtual inertia. Therefore, a discrete system frequency response (SFR) model considering VIC time delay is established in this paper. It is found through analysis that the frequency sampling period affects the critical stability condition much more sensitively than the time delay length. Furthermore, a sufficient condition for small-signal stability is proposed, which describes the upper limit of the virtual inertia of RESs by the frequency sampling period and the system inertia time constant. Although this condition is a conservative estimation of the upper limit of virtual inertia, the experiment on the test bench of RES-integrated power systems verifies that the sufficient condition is close to the critical condition. The sufficient condition is independent of the time delay length, making it more suitable for guiding practical engineering applications.

title: Enhancing PV Observability in Distribution Network via Dictionary Learning
abstract: The increasing presence of residential photovoltaic (PV) systems highlights the critical need for utilities to identify their location and configuration, such as capacity, azimuth and tilt. Yet utilities often lack reliable distributed PV information arising from incomplete or inconsistently updated records. To enhance the observability of smart inverter equipped PV systems located behind smart meters for inferring both their capacity and generation characteristics, this paper proposes a generalizable and interpretable framework using limited and distributed monitoring data. Motivated by the underlying shared features of distributed PV outputs, the method jointly captures common generation patterns and infers household-specific installation heterogeneity. We design a dictionary learning-based approach to efficiently derive standard PV profiles. We also propose an impact alignment matrix which integrates meteorological factors particularly global horizontal irradiance (GHI). Proposed learning approach and matrix design greatly enhance both the interpretability and forecasting performance of day-ahead PV generation. A numerically stable orthogonal dictionary structure further enables the disaggregation of community PV capacity by azimuth specific installation styles. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves accurate and adaptive estimation with low computational complexity, which provides practical benefits for PV management.

title: Protection of Series-Compensated Transmission Lines Connected to Inverter-Based Resources
abstract: The protection challenges and solutions for series-compensated transmission lines have been thoroughly investigated in the literature. In addition, many studies have highlighted the challenges posed by inverter-based resources (IBRs) to transmission line protection. However, the combined impacts of series compensation and IBRs on transmission line relays remain unexplored. This gap in research has significant practical implications, especially as inverter-based renewable energy sources are often located far from load centers, increasing the probability of series compensation in their vicinity. This paper investigates whether and how existing protection practices for series-compensated lines are influenced by the fault response of IBRs. The findings are relevant not only to the direct tie lines of IBRs but also to lines connected to parts of the grid where the generation is primarily inverter-based. The paper examines the distance and directional elements commonly used for transmission line protection. The analytical studies in this paper are supported by detailed PSCAD/EMTDC simulations of IBRs and series-compensated lines. The paper also presents comprehensive test results from commercial transmission line relays. The results demonstrate that the fault current characteristics of IBRs can invalidate key assumptions underlying existing protection solutions for series-compensated transmission lines, leading to potential misoperations of distance and directional elements. The paper identifies the root causes of these issues and discusses relay configuration strategies to achieve more reliable protection.

title: Optimal Frequency Trajectory-Guided Emergency Frequency Control for Receiving-End Grids
abstract: Aiming to enhance frequency support strength of receiving-end power grids, this paper presents an optimal frequency trajectory (OFT)-guided emergency frequency control strategy. The proposed methodology comprises three core components: First, an OFT-based system frequency response model is developed, incorporating wind farm frequency regulation characteristics while ensuring rotor speed self-recovery during primary frequency regulation. Second, a frequency support strength requirement evaluation model is established to determine necessary system inertia and frequency regulation capacity under frequency security limits. Third, a coordinated emergency frequency control strategy is proposed, enabling optimal power adjustment across multiple frequency regulation resources through virtual inertia and virtual droop parameter conversion. A dedicated compensation mechanism is integrated to address primary frequency regulation deadband effects. The effectiveness of the proposed models and control strategy is verified through comparative case studies using modified IEEE 39-bus and 118-bus test systems. Under the HVDC blocking scenario, the proposed approach reduces the maximum frequency deviation by 51.25% and achieves a cost-saving improvement of over 50% relative to the benchmarked existing methods.

title: Risk Assessment of Forced SSO Excited by DFIG-Originated Interharmonics
abstract: The forced subsynchronous oscillations (FSSOs) induced by the doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG)-originated interharmonics can degrade power quality and threaten the security of equipment as well as the power system. This study investigates the generation mechanisms of DFIG-originated interharmonics, and proposes a novel criterion of the impedance-based method that reveals the excitation mechanisms of FSSOs. Subsequently, a severity index for FSSOs, defined as the interharmonic amplitude ratio (IAR), is established to quantify the FSSO severity. A methodology is developed to compute the probability distribution of this severity function, incorporating the probabilistic characteristics of system operating conditions and wind speeds. Building upon this severity index and its probability distribution, a risk matrix integrating two distinct risk dimensions, power quality degradation risk and equipment/system security risks, is constructed to assess FSSO risk. The proposed methodology is validated through comprehensive time-domain simulations. Simulation results demonstrate that both risk types are highly sensitive to the probabilistic characteristics of grid operating conditions and wind speed profiles. Specifically, when the grid operates with high probability under weak-grid conditions, and the DFIG rotor frequency corresponding to average wind speed falls within 5/6∼7/6 times the fundamental frequency, the system experiences elevated levels of both FSSO-induced risks.

title: Robust Coordinated Prescriptive Power System Dispatch: Bridging Adjustable Robust OPF and Multiple Probabilistic Predictions
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable generation introduces substantial uncertainty into short-term power system operations, challenging cost-effective dispatch under network constraints. In conventional predict–then–optimize frameworks, uncertainty bounds are learned independently and treated as fixed inputs to robust optimal power flow (OPF), limiting feedback from operational decisions to improve uncertainty representation. This paper proposes a robust semi-end-to-end coordinated decision framework that bridges probabilistic forecasting and robust optimization for prescriptive power system dispatch. Probabilistic prediction models estimate one-step-ahead renewable generation and load intervals, which are incorporated into a robust OPF model through the induced uncertainty sets. The proposed framework integrates three components: a machine learning layer, a robust decision-making layer, and a decision evaluation layer. During the forward pass, predicted uncertainty bounds are converted into robust dispatch decisions, while in the backward pass, gradients are propagated through the optimization layer to train forecasting models using task-level operational feedback. Numerical results demonstrate stable training and consistent economic improvements over the conventional predict–then–optimize approach, achieving average total-cost reductions of 14.3% and 16.0% on the IEEE 5- and 30-bus systems, respectively. The improvement on the IEEE 118-bus system is smaller because uncertainty-related costs account for a limited portion of total operating costs. Under the adopted single-interval DC-based dispatch formulation, the proposed method also learns tighter uncertainty intervals (around 25% narrower) while reducing reserve-related slack activation under stressed operating conditions.

title: Distributed Control of Multi-Voltage-Level DC Microgrids for Resilient Renewable Interconnection
abstract: The dc microgrid (MG) has become an effective platform for integrating renewable energy sources (RESs) and energy storage systems, particularly in standalone configurations where local generation and loads are clustered. To enable complementary utilization of RESs across multiple islanded dc MGs, the triple active bridge converter (TABC) offers an attractive solution for interconnecting dc MGs with different voltage levels. This paper develops a distributed and resilient multi-port coordinated control strategy for TABC-interlinked dc MGs, enabling unified power regulation and fault-tolerant operation. The proposed method adapts seamlessly to various operating modes: it enables proportional power sharing among interconnected dc MGs under normal conditions, and it maintains uninterrupted power coordination through a consistent control scheme under fault conditions. This strategy enhances system resilience by ensuring continuous operation unaffected by faults while avoiding controller disturbances. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through hardware-in-the-loop experiments on a Typhoon-HIL platform.

title: Day-Ahead Scheduling of Hydrogen-Based Chemical Industry Park: A Bayesian Nonparametric Two-Sided Chance Constraint Method
abstract: Uncertainties introduced by renewable energy pose significant challenges to the scheduling of chemical industry parks that integrate an electricity-heat-hydrogen microgrid at the supply level and ammonia-based process chemical industry loads (APCILs) at the demand level. In this paper, a day-ahead scheduling framework based on Bayesian nonparametric two-sided chance constraint (BNTCC) is proposed to address these challenges. First, a refined operation model for electricity-heat-hydrogen microgrids and an integrated energy-material model for APCILs are developed, and the security constraints of hydrogen equipment and chemical production processes are incorporated. Second, a Dirichlet process mixture model (DPMM) is used to construct a Gaussian mixture (GM) distribution from historical uncertainty data to characterize renewable energy uncertainties. On the basis of this GM model, a two-sided chance constraint (TCC) scheduling method is proposed for the scheduling of chemical industry parks to reduce conservatism while ensuring that operational limits are jointly satisfied with a specified confidence level. Finally, to solve the TCC problem efficiently, a second-order cone programming (SOCP) formulation is derived using a piecewise linear (PWL) approximation. An additional algorithm is introduced to accelerate the computation by optimally selecting the PWL segments. Case studies illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for the day-ahead scheduling of chemical industry parks. Compared with state-of-the-art benchmark methods, the proposed method demonstrates superior cost effectiveness and computational efficiency.

title: Enhanced Frequency Regulation Utilizing Wind Power: Model Predictive Control Considering Adjustable Capacity of Wind Turbines
abstract: Random wind speed fluctuations can significantly influence a wind turbine's ability to release rotor kinetic energy during frequency regulation. To fully exploit the turbine's adjustable capacity, this paper establishes a dynamic model of a doubly fed induction generator and derives its adjustable capacity considering ultra-short-term wind speed forecasting. The nonlinear states are then projected into a high-dimensional linear space with the Koopman operator, enabling accurate global linearization. Based on this model, a distributed, capacity-aware Model Predictive Control (cVMPC) framework is formulated, where the ‘c’ denotes its core feature: capacity-awareness. To further improve performance, the adjustable capacity parameter is proactively predicted and incorporated into the MPC's control weighting coefficients. This enables an adaptive regulation strategy that explicitly accounts for the predicted kinetic energy reserves of each turbine. The proposed cVMPC approach is validated on a 3-machine, 9-bus system. Simulation results confirm that the strategy alleviates the initial frequency nadir, accelerates rotor speed recovery, and prevents secondary frequency dips.

title: Coordinated Interaction Between EV Charging Stations and Distribution Network via Stepwise Droop Control With SoC Interval Management
abstract: The flexible charging capability of electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) can improve distribution network (DN) operation with source-load uncertainties. To fully harness this potential, this paper proposes a three-stage coordinated interaction method between EVCSs and the DN, centered on a novel stepwise droop control function. In the first stage, a dynamic state of charge (SoC) interval management approach is introduced to determine the optimal SoC interval and the corresponding adjustable power interval for EVCSs, considering charging uncertainties and temporal coupling of energy. The second stage is implemented from the DN perspective using grid-wide information to optimize P-V stepwise droop control functions for EVCSs. To alleviate the computational burden from binary variables, a general binary reduction technique is adopted. In the last stage, each EVCS decomposes the obtained stepwise droop control function into multiple levels of charging power for individual EVs, considering the minimal changes in charging power and the satisfaction of target SoC. Consequently, in real time, the EVCS can self-regulate the charging power based on local voltage measurements. The simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed interaction method. Compared with the baseline method, it reduces the DN’s average voltage deviation and power loss by 13.29% and 14.68%, respectively.

title: Day-Ahead Wind Power Ramp Events Prediction With Extreme-Value–Driven Learning and Confidence-Aware Detection
abstract: Wind power ramp events (WPREs)—sudden, large-magnitude changes in wind generation—pose significant threats to power system stability. Accurate day-ahead prediction of WPREs is critical for proactive scheduling, reserve allocation, and grid security. However, existing methods often struggle with three key limitations: they underperform on rare and extreme events, lack sensitivity to multi-scale temporal dynamics, and provide little to no uncertainty quantification. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel day-ahead WPREs prediction method that integrates three innovations. First, we design an Extreme-Value-Driven Learning model that decomposes wind power into multiple temporal frequency bands, enabling the simultaneous capture of long-term trends and short-term changes. Second, we introduce a tailored extreme-based loss function that rebalances model learning from average-case accuracy toward greater sensitivity to ramp events. Third, we develop a wind power–oriented conformal inference method that produces model-adaptive confidence intervals with formal statistical guarantees, enabling a confidence-aware ramp detection algorithm. Unlike conventional approaches that prioritize mean error metrics, our method is tailored to the operational significance of ramp events. Remarkably, experimental results on two real-world wind power datasets show that our method improves WPREs prediction accuracy by up to 29.6% in terms of F1-score with negligible added computational cost.

title: Coordinated Optimization of Coupled Power–Traffic Networks: A Hierarchical SUE Method Considering Behavioral Preferences and Uncertainty
abstract: The rapid proliferation of electric vehicles intensifies the interdependence between transportation and power networks, posing operational challenges due to stochastic routing decisions and the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of charging demand. This paper proposes a hybrid decision-making framework that integrates user behavioral modeling with system-level optimization for coupled power-traffic networks. First, we develop network models that incorporate integrated energy stations (ESs) and heterogeneous vehicle classifications grouped by charging requirements and grid-response capabilities. Second, we formulate a hierarchical nested logit-based stochastic user equilibrium model to characterize multi-level user decisions under uncertainty. Furthermore, a collaborative power-traffic dispatch model is constructed to minimize generalized user costs, encompassing travel, charging, ES attributes, and power distribution network operation. A two-stage distributed solution algorithm is further developed to ensure computational tractability. Case studies on two test systems demonstrate the method's efficacy in characterizing user behavioral uncertainties and coordinating integrated power-traffic flows.

title: Rotor-Angle Stability Enhancement Control for MMC-MTDC Systems Without Sending-End Power Reserves
abstract: High-voltage direct current (HVDC) systems are increasingly integrated into AC grids, making rotor-angle stability more critical. Improper HVDC dynamics during disturbances may weaken synchronizing torque and damping, thereby aggravating oscillations. This paper investigates the offshore wind farm (OWF)-based multi-terminal DC (MTDC) system and analyzes the impact of its power injections on grid rotor-angle stability. On this basis, a frequency-based power control logic is first proposed to enhance rotor-angle stability. Building on this logic, Lyapunov-based control laws are derived to coordinate active and reactive power both among multiple terminals (inter-terminal level) and within each converter under capacity constraints (intra-terminal level). To further optimize the coordinated control, an optimization framework is then designed, ensuring effective and secure support. Finally, considering the absence of power reserves at the sending-end OWF, a capacitor energy-based control strategy is proposed for MTDC systems to utilize all MMCs’ capacitor energy at the same time for stability support (device level), thereby expanding the available support energy and further improving rotor-angle stability. The effectiveness and robustness of the proposed control are validated on the IEEE 39-bus system via PSCAD/EMTDC and MATLAB co-simulation.

title: Active Power Regulation of Wind Turbine Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning Guided Active Disturbance Rejection Control
abstract: Enhancing the active power regulation ability of wind turbine is a crucial approach to improving the flexibility of new power systems. This paper proposes a coordinated optimization strategy for reinforcement learning (RL) guided error-based active disturbance rejection controller (EADRC). Firstly, a well-established EADRC framework is employed, in which an extended state observer estimates and compensates for system disturbances in real time, thereby enhancing the system’s disturbance rejection capability and adaptability. Secondly, a Markovian decision process is integrated into the EADRC, allowing RL to adaptively tuning EADRC parameters in real time. This innovative integration of data-driven learning with disturbance rejection control enables the system to achieve optimal active power responses across diverse operating scenarios. Finally, simulations on a 5 MW wind turbine show that this proposed strategy outperforms conventional control methods in both active power tracking accuracy and system dynamic response, significantly enhancing the robustness of wind turbine control. This provides effective technical support for large-scale wind power integration in new power systems.

title: Multi-Mode Synchronization Control for Standalone Multi-Solar-Wind-Battery Storage System With Autonomous Transition and Improved Power Quality
abstract: This paper presents a modular distribution-level standalone microgrid topology and control strategy for remote-area applications, integrating multiple solar photovoltaic (SPV) arrays and variable-speed doubly fed induction generator (DFIG)–based wind energy systems. Proposed architecture supports coordinated operation of AC loads, low- and medium-voltage DC loads, and electric vehicle (EV) charging through a common DC bus, enhancing flexibility and scalability. In standalone operation, nonlinear and fluctuating loads, frequent mode transitions, and synchronization requirements to AC bus introduce significant stator harmonics and transient disturbances in DFIGs, leading to torque ripple, increased losses, and degraded efficiency with nonlinear loads. To address these challenges, a Versoria function–based zero-attraction least mean adaptive control is used to suppress harmonic distortion and ensure smooth autonomous operation. Proposed control enables seamless mode transitions and transient-free DFIG disconnection and reconnection. Real-time experimental validation confirms robust synchronization, enhanced power quality, and reliable performance under dynamic source and load variations.

title: Anticipatory Utility Operations With Long-Duration Hydrogen Storage and Carbon Market Synergies
abstract: When leveraged within carbon market mechanisms, hydrogen energy storage systems (HESS) offer a viable option for supporting low-carbon operation in vertically integrated utilities. However, a key challenge is that short-term operational decisions are made without explicit visibility of their long-term consequences, which are reflected through cumulative hydrogen and carbon constraints that ensure system feasibility. To bridge this time-scale gap, this paper proposes a reinforcement learning–augmented primal–dual rolling-horizon optimization framework. A trained future-aware regularizer incorporates long-term information into short-term decision-making, while a primal–dual scheme enforces cumulative constraints on hydrogen and carbon markets with computational tractability. Numerical studies on the IEEE 6-bus, 118-bus, and 300-bus test systems demonstrate the framework's effectiveness and scalability. Results demonstrate that the proposed framework keeps annual terminal residuals negligible while reducing peak emissions, improving economic performance, and enabling seasonal load shifting across different system scales.

title: Optimal Operation Strategy for AA-CAES in Joint Energy and Regulation Markets: Managing SoC Deviations From Regulation Response
abstract: As a representative technology of physical long-duration energy storage, advanced adiabatic compressed air energy storage (AA-CAES) is capable of providing joint energy and secondary frequency regulation (SFR) services, playing an important role in power system regulation. However, the nonlinear characteristics of AA-CAES poses a challenge, as tracking regulation signals induces shifts in the operating point and air consumption of AA-CAES, complicating the process for state-of-charge (SoC) management. This paper proposes an optimal operation strategy for AA-CAES in joint energy and SFR markets. First, the SoC deviation induced by regulation response of AA-CAES is analyzed, and a dynamic operation model for AA-CAES to provide joint energy and SFR capacity services incorporating deviation impacts is developed. Subsequently, a self-scheduling strategy accounting for the uncertainty of regulation signals is proposed. This strategy employs stochastic dynamic programming to construct value functions in the day-ahead stage, and develops a chance-constrained stochastic programming model for rolling optimization in the intra-day stage. Numerical simulations based on real-world AA-CAES plant data validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy. The results indicate that considering the SoC deviations increases the net revenue by 3.0%, while the adoption of chance constraints leads to net revenue increase of 4.3%.

title: Exploring the Flexibility of Twin-Basin Tidal Range Power Plants Through Optimal Control
abstract: In twin-basin tidal range schemes, a type of tidal barrage with two water reservoirs, the variations in sea water level throughout the day are used to generate electrical power, without direct CO2 emissions. This study focuses on optimising the operation of twin-basin tidal barrages using different objective functions, namely: energy maximising, income maximising and demand matching. The novelty of the study relies on using moment-based control to transcribe the infinite-dimensional twin-basin barrage optimal control problem into a finite-dimensional nonlinear program. To test the controller performance, a case study in the Severn Estuary, in the Southwest of the U.K., is presented, where the tidal resource is one of the highest in the world. It is found that, under tailored optimal scheduling, the twin-basin scheme can effectively shift generation periods to achieve greater income (between 1% and 3%, in the income maximising case) or to match peak demand hours (in the demand matching case), showing the increased flexibility of tidal range power plants compared to more traditional renewables. In the study cases presented, there is general agreement between energy maximising and demand matching optimal operation, since, for the particular time interval chosen, the phase of the tide was well aligned with demand, suggesting that tidal range plants are inherently demand-following. Furthermore, a control strategy is proposed for twin-basin barrages that results in continuous power output, reducing the hours of stand-by of the turbines, and highlighting the potential of twin-basin barrage for clean and dispatchable electricity generation.

title: Joint Optimization for Micro-Siting and Collector System of Floating Wind and Wave Energy Considering Stochastic Displacements Under Combined Wind-Wave-Current Loads
abstract: Co-locating floating wind turbines (FWTs) with wave energy converters (WECs) offers a promising pathway to reduce the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) for deep-sea renewable energy. However, stochastic platform displacements under coupled wind–wave–current loads aggravate wake interactions, degrade WEC shielding benefits, and increase cable fatigue risks—challenges not addressed by existing deterministic or empirical approaches. This paper proposes a bi-level distributionally robust optimization method for joint micro-siting and collector-system design of hybrid FWT–WEC plants. The upper level optimizes device layout by incorporating motion-aware wake–shielding coupling, while the lower level formulates a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model for cable topology, sizing, and slack allocation using Wasserstein ambiguity sets constructed via kernel density estimation. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed method reduces wake losses by 53.70%, FWT heave amplitude by 42.3%, cable length by 4.81%, line losses by 12.76%, and reliability costs by 39.55%, achieving an overall LCOE reduction of 5.36% compared to conventional approaches.

title: A Double-Machine Small-Signal Equivalence Method for Power Systems With GFL and GFM Converters via Eigenfunction Matching
abstract: Renewable power systems (RPSs) with both grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM) power electronic converters (PECs) have become prevalent. Complex dynamic interactions in RPSs pose analytical challenges on stability analysis. In such a context, this paper proposes an equivalent double-machine system (EDMS) and associated solution methods for analyzing small-signal stability issues of RPSs with both GFL and GFM PECs. Focusing on dominant modes, the original closed-loop system is first transformed into two Schur-complemented-form models that capture dominant modes introduced by GFL and GFM, respectively, then reduced via modal perturbation to equivalent single-machine subsystems (ESMSs), and finally, reconstructed into an EDMS that simultaneously captures the dominant modes introduced by both GFL and GFM PECs. The proposed method makes the most use of the equivalence of dominant eigenfunctions among the original system, the ESMSs, and the EDMS. Complementary solution approaches are developed for both white-box and black-box scenarios. The EDMS framework provides clear physical interpretability, i.e., a double-machine system, offering a scalable tool for dynamic analysis and stability evaluation in RPSs with GFL and GFM PECs.
