title: Regular Layout Optimization for Offshore Wind Farms Considering Seabed Terrains and Turbulence Intensity
abstract: The offshore wind farm layout optimization (OWFLO) is critical to effectively reducing energy costs. This study presents a planning method for the regular layout of OWF, considering both seabed terrains and turbulence intensity (TI), which is based on a mixed-integer linear fractional programming (MILFP) model. The proposed model considers the life-cycle costs of OWFs, including support structure costs, installation costs, and operation and maintenance (O&M) costs, in which the objective function aims to minimize the levelized cost of energy (LCOE). To address the computational challenges of large-scale OWFLO, we utilize the regular layouts’ “patterns” to reduce the dimensions of decision variables and simplify the power calculation constraints, so that the model can be decomposed and solved by the Bounded Dinkelbach Algorithm (BDA). Finally, the applicability of the proposed model on different terrains is validated through a real OWF in China.

title: Emulation of Ternary Pumped Storage Hydro Plants on a Laboratory Micro-Alternator
abstract: Ternary Pumped Storage Hydro (T-PSH) plant, a structural innovation of conventional PSH (C-PSH) plant, is a vital and reliable energy storage technology that plays a critical role in modern power systems. In this paper, an experimental emulator is developed to effectively mimic the mechanical and electrical behavior of the T-PSH plants, using a laboratory micro-alternator coupled to a DC motor. Detailed models of the excitation system, hydro-governor, and nonlinear shared penstock models of the hydro-turbine and pump are used to emulate operational behavior during the Generation, Pumping, and Hydraulic Short-Circuit (HSC) modes of the T-PSH plant. The IEEE PES Power System Dynamic Performance Committee recommended models of the T-PSH plant are adopted in this paper for emulation purposes. A novel emulation framework is developed in which the DC motor, controlled via a bi-directional IGBT-based power electronic converter, is used to accurately emulate the governor–turbine and pump dynamics of the T-PSH plant. The micro-alternator H-bridge excitation system is controlled to emulate the T-PSH generator-exciter dynamics. An inertia constant ($H$) regulator and a time constant ($T^{\prime }_{do}$) regulator are implemented to emulate the different inertia and large field time constants of the T-PSH plants. The developed emulator is tested on a laboratory single-machine infinite bus (SMIB) system. The experimental results are compared with the time-domain simulations performed in MATLAB/Simulink to substantiate the proposed methodology, demonstrating the micro-alternator's capability to emulate T-PSH dynamics under different modes of operation for both small and large signal disturbances.

title: Pre-Trained Invertible Neural Network Assisted High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization Framework for Wind Farm Layout Design
abstract: Wake effects in wind farms degrade energy capture and turbine reliability, underscoring the importance of layout optimization. Existing studies either rely on analytical wake models at the expense of accuracy or combine numerical wake models with heuristic algorithms at the expense of efficiency. In contrast, we propose a pre-trained invertible neural network-assisted high-dimensional Bayesian optimization framework for wind farm layout design, achieving both high accuracy and high efficiency. Specifically, this study employs a high-fidelity numerical wake model to ensure accurate wake estimation and develops a Bayesian optimization (BO)–based framework to enhance search efficiency. An invertible neural network (INN) is specifically designed and, for the first time, integrated with BO to alleviate the curse of dimensionality in high-dimensional layout spaces. The proposed INN-BO framework is evaluated under five distinct and progressively complex scenarios, including the real offshore data from California. Comparative evaluations against state-of-the-art algorithms demonstrate that INN-BO achieves superior solution quality with reduced convergence time, highlighting its strong generalizability and practical relevance to real-world wind farm design.

title: Event-Driven Restoration of Interconnected Distribution Systems With R-SOPs Adapting to Continuous Disasters and Uncertainties
abstract: Extreme disasters lead to continuous and large-scale faults in distribution systems (DSs), posing challenges in developing practical restoration strategies. This paper proposes a pre-disaster prevention and post-disaster restoration framework for R-SOP-enabled interconnected distribution systems (IDSs), which accounts for the persistence of faults during evolution and the uncertainties in renewable energy source and load. Unlike most existing studies that focus on individual DSs and fixed fault scenarios, this paper employs a reconfigurable soft open point (R-SOP) with asymmetric converter design. Through its feeder selection and converter reconfiguration mechanisms, the R-SOP enables efficient capacity utilization and dynamic interconnection among multiple DSs, and additionally addresses, in a unified manner, the dual uncertainties of stochastic fluctuations and sudden faults under continuous disasters. In the pre-disaster phase, electric buses (EBs) are deployed based on proactive restoration simulations to reduce potential load shedding and shorten post-disaster travel distances. In the post-disaster phase, an event-driven restoration method is developed, wherein predefined fault events and error events dynamically update restoration strategies to adapt to continuous faults and uncertainties. By combining R-SOP-assisted reconfiguration with coordinated scheduling of flexible resources, the proposed method overcomes the limitations of individual-network restoration, enhancing system resilience. Simulation results based on a modified 102-node IDS show that the proposed method not only accelerates service restoration under continuous extreme disaster events but also ensures voltage security.

title: Power Coupling Mechanism Analysis and Hierarchical Adaptive Decoupling Control for Wind Farm Connected to Weak Grid
abstract: Active frequency and voltage support from wind turbine generators (WTGs) improves grid stability. However, when connected to weak grid, phase-locked loop (PLL) tracking inaccuracies can cause inadequate power decoupling in WTGs. This issue is further aggravated by uneven wind speeds and spatial structure within wind farm (WF), ultimately undermining overall support capability. To address this problem, this paper firstly systematically investigates the influence of multiple factors on the coupling power from the unit, farm, to grid levels. Specifically, PLL bandwidth and grid strength affect the tracking performance of the PLL, while wind speed distribution and spatial structure influence the operating points of WTGs and the coupling transmission between nodes, respectively. On the basis, the Hierarchical Adaptive Decoupling Control (HADC) strategy for WF is proposed, which mitigate the coupling power by introducing quantified power coupling components into the power outer-loop control of rotor-side converter. To improve the applicability and robustness, the main parameters of HADC adaptively vary according to load changes and wind speed distribution. It enables to reduce the power coupling degree and improve frequency and voltage support capability of WF. Finally, case studies are conducted on a real WF project in Bazhou, Xinjiang, China. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

title: Prediction-Based Interval Voltage Regulation Involving PV-BESS Coordination
abstract: Modern distribution networks face critical voltage security challenges due to high penetration of photovoltaic (PV) systems and battery energy storage systems (BESSs). Traditional regulation strategies have proven inadequate in mitigating rapid voltage violations caused by power fluctuations. Therefore, a prediction-based proportional coordinated power compensation method is proposed for interval voltage regulation (VR). Firstly, an improved convolutional neural network model is established to predict variable power flows by considering PV and load characteristics, enabling accurate voltage profile prediction. Then, the crucial bus with the most voltage violation is identified, and the optimal coordination ratios for reactive power compensation (RPC) and active power compensation (APC) are determined by an optimization process based on dynamic sensitivity analysis. Furthermore, the crucial bus VR method sequentially allocates RPC from PV inverters and APC from BESSs using a sensitivity-based proportional coordination. Finally, the test results demonstrate an effective VR across all buses over a 24-hour operation, with total RPC and APC requirements reduced by 41.8% and 34.5% in a real 10-bus network, and by 79.1% and 39.5% in the IEEE 123-bus network, respectively.

title: An LVRT Strategy for DFIG-BESS Based WECS With Maximum Voltage Support
abstract: The regional grid codes mandate that wind energy conversion systems (WECSs) stay connected during grid faults as long as terminal voltages stay above a specified level with respect to the fault duration. While existing low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) strategies for DFIG-WECSs satisfy these requirements, they do not guarantee maximum AC bus voltage recovery, which is essential for maintaining grid connectivity during severe faults. This paper presents an LVRT strategy for an on-grid DFIG supplying an AC microgrid. Rotor and stator overcurrent in the initial fault stage are limited using a crowbar. Then, a proposed coordinated RSC-GSC control aligns the DFIG-stator and transformer HV-side currents, maximizing the resultant AC bus injected current. Next, a modified adaptive voltage support scheme further maintains optimal real-time d-q axis current ratios for both converters (utilizing full capacity), so that overall injected current matches the network X/R ratio, ensuring maximum voltage recovery, regardless of the fault level, duration, location, wind speed, and wind farm condition. OPAL-RT real-time simulations confirm a 5.90% improvement in AC-bus voltage recovery and an 82% enhancement in post-fault transient response over recent literature.

title: Optimal Volt-VAR Curve Design for Inverter-Based Resources in Distribution Grids
abstract: The electric distribution grid has undergone rapid evolution, with customers increasingly adopting distributed energy resources (DERs). Conventional grid devices, like static reactive power compensators, were installed to address specific operational needs under traditional load conditions and are often not automated, making them less effective in today’s dynamic grid. Uncoordinated DER operation can further exacerbate issues, causing overvoltage, reverse reactive power flow, substation congestion, and low load power factor (LPF), highlighting the limitations of legacy grid assets. This paper presents an innovative methodology to design optimal volt-VAR curves (VVCs) for inverters to mitigate these challenges. To facilitate convergence and accelerate the computation of the optimal power flow (OPF) problem, a linear three-phase network power flow solver is employed to minimize reactive power flow through the substation and enhance the voltage profile within the distribution grid. Unlike existing approaches that use static VVCs or determine VVCs for each time instant, the proposed method generates an optimal VVC for each PV inverter over a specified period, while also producing location-specific curves. The approach is demonstrated on the IEEE 123-Node feeder and a large-scale real feeder with multiple PV inverters, showing improvements in substation LPF and feeder voltage profiles.

title: EMT-EMT Co-Simulation for Large-Scale Offshore Wind Integration in the New York State Grid
abstract: The rapid integration of large-scale offshore wind (OSW) farms and inverter-based resources (IBRs) presents unprecedented challenges for power system stability and protection. While electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation provides the necessary fidelity to capture fast control interactions, modeling an entire regional grid alongside detailed OSW models exceeds the computational capacity of single real-time simulators. This paper presents the practical design, implementation, and validation of a distributed real-time EMT–EMT co-simulation framework to evaluate the integration of 9 GW of offshore wind into the New York State (NYS) power grid. By interfacing heterogeneous real-time simulators of RTDS and OPAL-RT via an Aurora-based fiber-optic communication link and a Transmission Line Model (TLM), the computational burden is effectively distributed. A comprehensive experimental evaluation is conducted, including a direct comparison between analog and fiber-optic interconnections. The results demonstrate that the Aurora-based fiber interface significantly improves latency, synchronization accuracy, and transient waveform fidelity compared to traditional analog setups. Ultimately, this application study demonstrates how the proposed framework overcomes the limitations of traditional interfaces, enabling high-fidelity, real-time stability assessment of the NYS grid under severe fault conditions and providing actionable insights to de-risk large-scale OSW deployment.

title: An Enhanced Grid-Forming Control Strategy for DC-Coupled Alkaline Water Electrolyzers
abstract: Recent years have seen the research on the participation of Alkaline water electrolyzers (AWEs) in power grid regulation gained significant traction. In particular, the participation of AWEs in grid-forming (GFM) services is precisely an urgent research topic at present. However, regarding the involvement of AWEs in GFM services, existing studies are typically limited to single AWE units or rely on communication for controlling multiple AWEs. Nor have they considered the capacity variation characteristics of AWEs. Furthermore, the unique topologies of DC-coupled AWE systems require special consideration. To address these issues, this paper proposes an enhanced GFM control strategy for DC-coupled AWE systems. Specifically, the proposed control scheme includes two key improvements. First, a temperature-driven droop control is employed to enable coordinated operation among individual AWE units. Second, an improved DC-link voltage synchronized control (IDVSC) is proposed for the voltage source converter (VSC). Furthermore, the proposed strategy is fully decentralized, allowing both AWE units and the VSC to provide GFM services. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed strategy is validated through simulation and experimental results.

title: A Distributed Two-Stage Framework for the Co-Scheduling of Power, Heat and Hydrogen Networks With Heterogeneous Frequency Supports
abstract: This paper proposes a distributed two-stage framework for the co-scheduling of power, heat and hydrogen networks with primary and enhanced frequency supports. To address the bilinear terms inherent in the Nadir frequency constraint, a distributed two-stage framework in the form of a fully-distributed computational pipeline is proposed. In the first stage, FedOnce, a distributed learning architecture with one-shot communication, is proposed to coordinate the energy sectors to efficiently predict the total frequency reserves. These predictions serve as warm starts to generate accurate linearizations of the bilinear Nadir terms, which are then embedded into the second-stage convex optimization of power, heat and hydrogen networks through the decentralized alternating-direction method of multipliers with pre-keyed encryption. The underlying distributed computational pipeline helps resolve the dilemma between computational efficiency and information privacy, through both parallel learning and advanced encryption. Case studies demonstrate its significant improvements in computational efficiency (by 2 orders of magnitude), approximation gaps (by 4.2%) and frequency response characteristics.

title: Distributed Adaptive Coordination of Flexibility Resources for Real-Time Power Balancing in Islanded DC Microgrids
abstract: Modern DC microgrids (DC-MGs) typically incorporate Renewable Energy Sources (RESs), energy storage systems, and local loads. In islanded DC-MGs, effective coordination of these components is essential for secure and reliable operation, given the intermittent nature of RESs and the uncertain demand profile. This paper employs electric spring topology to enhance flexibility through the smart management of both energy stored in batteries, and loads, in the case that the generation capacity of multiple RESs—operating with the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm—is insufficient to meet demand. Besides, a distributed adaptive droop-based scheme is designed concerning a trade-off between common bus voltage regulation and proper current/power sharing among units. This distributed scheme benefits from a low-bandwidth communication interface among the in-service units to collect required data for adaptive estimation of droop gains. To ensure reliable operation of the DC-MG, batteries' capacity and State-of-Charge (SoC) information are also incorporated into the energy-sharing strategy, aiming to maintain SoC balance among storage units during replenishment. The feasibility of the proposed approach is evaluated through a Power-Hardware-in-the-Loop (PHIL) platform.

title: Hybrid Fault Isolation and Power Control of Wind Turbine Generators Based on Stacked UIO
abstract: The stable operation of megawatt-class wind turbines directly impacts grid connection performance. As complex electromechanicald systems operating in variable environments, time-varying hybrid faults frequently occur, posing challenges for fault-tolerant control (FTC). This paper proposes novel approaches for hybrid fault diagnosis and fault-tolerant controller design. First, a collaborative architecture for a stacked unknown input observer (UIO) is constructed for integrated fault diagnosis of hybrid faults in wind turbine generators (WTGs). The designed stacked UIO strategy can decouple and separately estimate the dynamic of speed and torque, achieving effective time-varying hybrid fault diagnosis. Second, given the disturbances, uncertainties, and discrete-time nature of WTGs, the asymptotic stability of the proposed UIO is established using Lyapunov’s theorem. Finally, combining fault information, a two-degree-of-freedom model predictive control strategy is adopted to achieve FTC while also considering power stability tracking. Simulation results show that the proposed method can estimate time-varying faults in WTG actuators and sensors, and maintain reliable control performance under hybrid fault conditions, thereby verifying its effectiveness as a comprehensive FTC solution.

title: Multi-objective Non-causal Optimal Control of an Active Pumping System for a Floating Wind Platform
abstract: Semi-submersible floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs) are susceptible to undesirable wave- and wind-induced pitch motion which may be reduced by control strategies. Presently these mainly rely on passive damping, which becomes ineffective under varying sea states. To address this issue, this paper proposes an active pumping strategy for water ballast using multi-objective noncausal optimal controller to suppress pitch motion by pumping water among three columns, thereby generating a counteracting moment against wave and wind excitations. Firstly, the dynamic model of the triple-column VolturnUS floating platform, coupled with hydrodynamic and aerodynamic forces, is developed using the Euler–Lagrange method. Based on this model, a multi-objective noncausal optimal controller is developed to balance pitch motion suppression and pumping power. When pitch minimization is prioritized, compared with the conventional passive damping control, the proposed method reduces the pitch motion by 85% but with high power demand. When power consumption is penalized, the controller can still reduce the pitch by 82% while lowering power usage by 95%, indicating a trade-off between motion suppression and pump energy consumption.

title: OLSchedLM: Leveraging Language Model for Economically-Driven and Curve-Aware Microgrid Online Scheduling Optimization
abstract: Online scheduling of microgrids is crucial for enhancing economic efficiency and stability. However, traditional model-based methods rely on accurate forecasts. Among data-driven approaches, reinforcement learning is constrained by training instability. Meanwhile, although imitation learning can learn policies directly from expert trajectories, conventional architectures suffer from limited sequence modeling capabilities and severe data hunger. To address these, this paper leverages the synergistic benefits of advanced architecture and inherent generalization capability of language models (LM). Specifically, we propose an online scheduling method based on LM named OLSchedLM, which adapts LM to this complex, continuous-control task. We frame the scheduling problem as a conditional sequence modeling task and train the LM-based agent on expert trajectories. These trajectories are generated by solving a bi-level programming model that incorporates domain knowledge and is designed to co-optimize electricity trading income and net load peak-valley difference. To pioneer a numerical-to-numerical paradigm, a suite of key adaptation techniques is introduced to bridge the domain gap between language and numerical control, including input and output projection layers and a two-stage parameter-efficient fine-tuning process. Extensive experiments demonstrate that OLSchedLM significantly outperforms established methods. Crucially, OLSchedLM’s excellent performance in few-shot experiments validates its effectiveness in addressing data hunger issue.

title: Negative-Sequence Impedance Provision of a Virtual Admittance-Based Inverter-Based Resource
abstract: While some grid-forming (GFM) inverter-based resources (IBRs) have both positive- and negative-sequence control units equipped to provide desired negative-sequence impedance, we find that a virtual admittance-based GFM-IBR with only positive-sequence unit can also provide desired negative-sequence impedance for grid code compliance. The goal of this paper is to provide an analysis to relate the negative-sequence impedance provision with the control scheme. To this end, an electromagnetic transient (EMT) testbed is developed to examine an IBR’s behavior subject to unbalanced grid faults. The negative-sequence voltage and current components are measured to calculate the equivalent negative-sequence impedance empirically. It is found that this impedance is indeed associated with the virtual impedance. The underlying mechanism is further discovered through complex vector-based analysis and frame conversion. The major takeaways are two-fold: (i) For a given control scheme, its negative-sequence impedance can be found analytically; (ii) inverter control can be designed more concisely to provide both positive- and negative-sequence impedances, in contract of having more complicated design with both positive- and negative-sequence control units included.

title: Graph Neural Network With Dual-Stream Attention for Global Maximum Power Point Tracking Under Partial Shading Conditions
abstract: Due to the complex nonlinear coupling between circuit topology and environmental changes, precise maximum power point tracking under partial shading conditions remains a challenge. Existing data-driven methods typically view photovoltaic (PV) arrays as unstructured feature vectors or Euclidean grids, which fail to capture the fundamental series-parallel constraints that control the distribution of current and voltage. This study proposes a graph neural network with dual-stream attention (GNN-DSA), which is a physical perception framework that can strictly decouple static topologies from dynamic environmental signals. Static streams encode arrays into message-passed directed graphs with specific edge types that capture series-parallel circuit constraints, while dynamic streams capture irradiation patterns through the Transformer. A novel bidirectional cross-attention mechanism explicitly simulates the interaction between circuit constraints and environmental stress. Hardware verification indicates that the tracking efficiency of GNN-DSA on real PV panels is 99.1%–99.6%, on solar array simulators is 99.99%, and the response time is less than 100 ms. Comparative analysis shows that compared with the multilayer perceptron baseline, GNN-DSA reduces the mean squared error by 45.6%, and compared with the state-of-the-art Crossformer model, it reduces it by 22.3%.

title: Stability Analysis and Parametric Feasible-Region Characterization of Multi-Oscillation Modes in GFL-GFM Hybrid Systems Under Wide Scale Grid Strength
abstract: This paper investigates the stability of multi-low-frequency oscillation (LFO) modes in grid-connected hybrid systems with grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM) converters. The objective is to reveal the coupling oscillation mechanism between dual-source power and control parameters under wide variations in grid strength, and to construct a stable operating domain. A reduced-order model balancing accuracy and complexity is established, and a decoupled equivalent damping analysis method is proposed to quantitatively characterize the stability of the dominant GFL and GFM oscillation modes from the perspective of damping formation mechanism. It is found that the GFL-dominated and GFM-dominated oscillation modes exhibit opposite stability evolution trends with respect to grid strength and are constrained by the dual-source power coupling effect. As a result, a single fixed parameter set cannot ensure stable system operation across a wide range of grid strengths and full power operating conditions. Furthermore, the influence of key control parameters on the oscillation modes is clarified, and stable parameter boundaries under extreme operating conditions are determined. Time-domain simulations validate the accuracy of the theoretical analysis and the proposed stable domain construction method.

title: Dual-Port DC Wind Turbines Based Offshore Wind Power Integration System Embedded With Power Balance and Fault Ride-Through Capability
abstract: In offshore wind farm (OWF) integration systems, emerging DC collection and transmission schemes (all-DC) necessitate the series-parallel connection of DC wind turbines (WTs) to boost the DC collection voltage. However, power imbalance among DC WTs impairs the overall efficiency of the integration system. To address the inherent limitations of the all-DC approach, this paper proposes a dual-port DC wind turbine-based DC collection and transmission topology for OWF integration. Where the DC ports of each DC WT are connected in series to elevate the DC collection voltage, while the AC ports of adjacent DC WTs are connected to decouple the power of DC WTs. Firstly, the topology, operating principle and control strategy of the all-DC integration system incorporating the proposed DC WT are introduced, and the power balance mechanism is analyzed. Then, a comprehensive fault ride-through (FRT) method is proposed to handle various fault types. Furthermore, the parameter design method and overall evaluation of the proposed integration system are conducted. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed all-DC integration system under different operation scenarios is validated in PSCAD/EMTDC.

title: Regulating Hydrothermal Deposition Kinetics via an Acid–Base Buffering Strategy for Efficient HTL-Free Sb2Se3 Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The hydrothermal method, known for its operational simplicity, environmental benignity, and low cost, has been established as a viable route for fabricating high-efficiency antimony selenide (Sb2Se3) photovoltaic devices. However, the closed nature of this system poses a significant challenge to gaining an intuitive and comprehensive understanding of the underlying reaction mechanisms during hydrothermal deposition. In this work, we reveal a “self-accelerating” phenomenon that occurs during the selenium releasing process from the sodium selenosulfate (Na2SeSO3) selenium precursor. To address this issue, this work introduced an HAc/Na2SO3 buffering pair to regulate the hydrothermal chemistry, thereby achieving controlled release of HSe- species. The introduction of the buffer additive promotes the heterogeneous nucleation of Sb2Se3 on the substrate and prolongs the sustained release of the Se source, enabling a thicker film with distinctly strengthened enhanced (221) and (301) crystallographic orientations. The resulting Sb2Se3 solar cell without a hole transport layer delivers a champion power conversion efficiency of 6.77%. Overall, this work expands the possibilities for manipulating reaction pathways in solution-based deposition from a chemical perspective.

title: Frequency-Sharing Scheme for IPC-CSC Offshore Wind MTDC Systems Using Logistic Function
abstract: The current source converter-based multi-terminal DC (CSC-MTDC) system with improved phase control (IPC) method provides a promising solution for transmitting offshore wind power to multiple AC grids. However, the AC voltage control mechanism of such systems has not been fully investigated, and the inherent DC decoupling characteristics make it difficult to suppress frequency disturbances caused by wind speed fluctuations. To address these issues, this paper establishes the mathematical model of the IPC-CSC and proposes an offshore AC voltage control strategy by constructing intermediate variables, thereby ensuring the stable operation of the overall system. Furthermore, a frequency-sharing coordinated control strategy is proposed, where independent power and frequency control loops and voltage compensation are introduced. Thus, multiple receiving AC systems can jointly share power disturbances and fully utilize frequency regulation resources. In addition, an adaptive droop control method based on a logistic function is designed to provide smooth and bounded frequency support under different levels of frequency deviation. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategies is validated through simulation and hardware-in-the-loop experiment results.

title: A Hybrid Interpretable Reinforcement Learning Framework for Robust Pitch Control of Large-Scale Wind Turbines
abstract: The increasing size and structural flexibility of offshore wind turbines (WTs) give rise to complex multi-modal dynamics and strong aeroelastic coupling, which render accurate control-oriented modelling impractical for large-scale turbines. While deep reinforcement learning (RL) offers a promising model-free alternative for pitch control, its application to large WTs remains challenged by training stability, safety, and limited interpretability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a model-free, safety-oriented, and interpretable RL-based pitch control framework for large-scale WTs. A hybrid architecture is developed by embedding a gain-scheduled PI (GSPI) baseline within a residual RL structure, together with a smooth damping mechanism to ensure stable learning. In addition, a SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based module is incorporated to interpret the learned policy through feature importance and time-resolved control patterns. Simulation results in OpenFAST using a 15 MW monopile WT demonstrate over 23% reductions in generator speed and power fluctuations under the nominal training scenario, together with mitigated tower and blade fatigue loads. Additional robustness evaluations under high-turbulence operating conditions further confirm that the proposed method maintains strong performance relative to the benchmark, and support safe, robust, and interpretable pitch control for large-scale WTs.

title: Lyapunov Compatibility-Based Adaptive Consensus Algorithm in PV-BESS Integrated Island DC Microgrids: A Dynamic State of Charge Balancing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel State-of-Charge (SoC)-based power allocation strategy for photovoltaic (PV)-based DC microgrids, leveraging an adaptive consensus algorithm to ensure SoC balance across Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) nodes. The primary control scheme employs inner-loop current droop control to mitigate disturbances arising from PV operation. The SoC-based power allocation strategy serves as a secondary control mechanism, designed to maintain a uniform SoC level across all BESS nodes via the adaptive consensus algorithm. This algorithm is compatible with a range of secondary control types, thereby mitigating battery degradation. Specifically, the stability and compatibility of the SoC-based power allocation strategy are rigorously proven by constructing a Lyapunov function. The proposed control strategy is simulated in MATLAB/SIMULINK and in an OPAL-RT-based real-time simulation environment to demonstrate its effectiveness, in which the proposed adaptive consensus algorithm can accommodate two different secondary control strategies.

title: Are Mechanisms Important for AI to Identify Oscillation Sources? A Case Study
abstract: Grid-connected wind turbine generators (WTGs) may induce sub-synchronous oscillations (SSOs) in a power system. Due to the difficulty to gain the detailed parameters of the WTGs in practice, data-driven AI method is considered to be a potential solution to identify the trouble-making WTGs (or SSO sources) in the power system. Unlike the SSO mechanism observed in traditional power systems, numerous studies and real-world SSO events have indicated that the SSO mechanisms in wind power grid-connected systems can be more complex and varied. However, most AI-based works ignore the fact that the SSO can arise from different mechanisms. Typically, AI models are trained and evaluated using data generated from a single type of SSO mechanism. However, in practice, AI models may need to identify the sources of SSOs caused by different or even unknown mechanisms. This raises an interesting question: Are mechanisms important for AI to identify oscillation sources? This paper provides a preliminary exploration of this question through a specific case study that examines two general SSO mechanisms: negative resistance and open-loop modal resonance. Further explainability analysis is carried out to investigate whether the SSO mechanisms affect the performance of the AI models. Results of study cases and explainability analysis provide researchers and engineers with deeper insights into the generalization ability of AI with respect to SSO mechanisms.

title: Lightweight Series-Connected Topology and Control Strategy for Megawatt-Scale High-Altitude Wind Energy Systems
abstract: Scaling high-altitude wind energy systems (HAWESs) to the megawatt level faces a “weight–voltage” paradox: reducing tether mass requires medium voltage, yet conventional voltage-boosting components add prohibitive airborne mass. This paper resolves the paradox with a novel architecture using series-connected, diode-rectified generators, which inherently builds medium transmission voltage without onboard converters or transformers, enabling an ultralight airborne system controlled solely by a grid-side converter (GSC) located on the ground. A small-signal stability analysis considering generator parameter heterogeneity reveals that the system is robust to moderate wind variations, but becomes unstable when wind-speed heterogeneity drives a turbine into a region of positive torque–speed slope. The precise identification of this physical stability boundary provides the crucial design guidance needed to unlock a practical pathway toward the deployment of utility-scale HAWESs.

title: Stability Analysis of Grid-Forming Inverter-Based Resources Using Sequence Immittance Modeling and Dual Feedback Loop Criteria
abstract: Sequence immittance framework is an effective method to analyze the frequency-domain stability between the inverter-based resource (IBR) and the grid. However, there is a lack of a generic sequence immittance stability analysis framework for grid-forming inverter-based resource (GFM-IBR) considering frequency coupling and AC-DC coupling simultaneously. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a stability analysis framework for GFM-IBR using sequence immittance modeling and dual feedback loop criteria. Firstly, GFM-IBR is definitely modeled as impedance with self-stabilization based on two-port network by standardizing the immittance form for frequency coupling and AC-DC coupling. Secondly, the dual feedback loop criterion, integrating frequency coupling and AC-DC coupling, is proposed to avoid the need of checking the right-half-plane (RHP) poles. Finally, cases of grid-connected GFM-IBR verify the correctness of the proposed stability analysis framework. It is revealed that the voltage loop is the main reason for GFM self-stabilization, which enables GFM-IBR to be modeled in impedance form. Frequency coupling and AC-DC coupling greatly affect the stability of GFM-IBR as short circuit ratio (SCR) increases, which should not be neglected. The nonlinearity in synchronization and control of GFM-IBR affects frequency and AC-DC coupling more than that of grid-following inverter-based resource (GFL-IBR), while both exhibit dual uniformity.

title: Optimal Planning of Offshore Wind Farm Collector System Considering Intensive Sea Use
abstract: Driven by the global clean energy transition, the offshore wind power has been expanding rapidly worldwide. In offshore wind farms (OWFs), the electrical collector system (ECS) already accounts for a substantial portion of the total project cost, while emerging sea-use regulations call for compact, corridor-based cable layouts instead of traditional dispersed radial schemes. This paper proposes an OWF-ECS planning framework tailored to the intensive use of sea areas. We formulate a mixed-integer linear programming model (MILP) that incorporates the requirement of the intensive sea-use and uses the parallel-laying length of cables to represent spatial intensification. A clustering-based warm-start strategy and distance-based candidate-arc reduction are further designed to improve solution efficiency and scalability. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed framework can accommodate diverse sea-use requirements and intensification levels, consistently generating economically efficient and spatially intensive ECS layouts and obtaining high-quality feasible or optimal solutions within acceptable computation time.

title: Adaptive Perceptual Graph Learning for Robust Wind Power Forecasting Under Incomplete Observations
abstract: Reliable wind power forecasting plays a crucial role in enabling efficient scheduling and effective energy management in virtual power plants. However, incomplete data observations caused by sensor malfunctions and volatile environmental conditions significantly compromise the reliability of wind power forecasting. To address these challenges, this paper presents a robust adaptive perceptual graph learning framework designed to enhance forecasting accuracy and robustness. The proposed framework uses an attention-gated GRU encoder to restore spatiotemporal dependencies under incomplete observations and integrates an adaptive graph convolution module to dynamically capture complex, non-stationary spatial correlations between wind turbines. To further promote physical consistency, a physics-informed discriminator is introduced as a plug-in component, guiding the model to align its outputs with the nonlinear aerodynamic relationship between wind speed and power generation. In addition, a sensitivity-aware adjustment strategy is developed to dynamically emphasize low-speed operating regimes. Comprehensive experiments conducted on real-world wind farm datasets show that the proposed method consistently surpasses baseline approaches, achieving a reduction of up to 35% in mean absolute percentage error, even under severe missing data scenarios.

title: Knowledge-Data-Driven-Based Feasible Region of Frequency Regulation Parameter for Wind Farm
Wind Speed Scenario Generation Under Typhoon Conditions via Prediction-Anchored Diffusion
abstract: Wind speed sequences under typhoon conditions exhibit complex spatio-temporal non-stationary characteristics, making it challenging for existing methods to control key features. This paper proposes a method for generating conditional wind speed scenarios based on a prediction-anchored diffusion model (PADM). First, a typhoon-aware time-series graph neural network (TA-TGNN) is developed, which constructs typhoon-aware adjacency matrices through trajectory similarity, temporal decay, and intensity similarity to characterize non-stationary dependencies. Second, a dual-dimensional adaptive attention mechanism (DDAM) is introduced, combining phase detectors and physical constraints to adaptively select and fuse key information across temporal and feature dimensions, thereby enhancing phase-aware prediction. Finally, PADM leverages deterministic prediction results as anchors and integrates hierarchical conditional encoding with temporal awareness to generate physically consistent and diverse wind speed scenarios. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed method accurately reproduces the structural characteristics of typhoon wind speeds and captures variations under different conditions, while maintaining stability and consistency across various hyperparameter settings.

title: Multi-Source Coordinated Frequency Control of Grid-Connected Wind-Solar-Storage Power Station With Economic Improvement
abstract: Renewable power plant participating in frequency regulation often compromises power generation efficiency, and existing frequency regulation strategies generally neglect economic cost. To improve frequency security and economic efficiency, the paper proposes a multi-source coordinated frequency control (MCFC) for wind-solar-storage hybrid power stations. The MCFC control consists of two stages: frequency support and frequency recovery. During frequency support, photovoltaic (PV), wind, and energy storage are sequentially activated according to dynamic characteristics. The strategy allocates wind, PV, and energy storage outputs based on frequency security constraints to avoid excessive use of regulation energy and improve economic efficiency. During frequency recovery, wind turbine rotor speed is smoothly restored, and the recovery of the energy storage system (ESS) state of charge (SOC) is explicitly considered. Case studies are undertaken on the two-area power system with a wind-solar-storage hybrid power station and Guangshui hybrid collection station. The results show that MCFC can restore the frequency above safety thresholds and minimize renewable regulation energy to improve economic efficiency. Compared with existing methods, MCFC not only restores frequency to 49.5 Hz under a wider range of disturbances but also reduces economic index by up to 40% under mild disturbances.

title: HyMoOpt: A Hybrid Momentum Optimizer for Axial Induction Factor Control of Wind Farm Under Dynamic Wake Effects
abstract: This paper addresses the real-time axial induction factor (AIF) control problem for large-scale wind farms under dynamic wake effects and uncertain wind conditions. We first establish the mathematical formulation for the AIF control problem. The objective is to optimize collective power output while balancing the trade-off between energy revenue and the degradation of turbine lifespan caused by AIF adjustments. Building upon this foundation, we propose a novel hybrid momentum optimizer (HyMoOpt) controller. It combines a model-based gradient estimator for rapid convergence with a model-free feedback mechanism for robustness against model mismatch. A momentum term is further integrated to accelerate convergence and damp oscillations. We then derive an analytical bound on the gradient approximation error and prove that the proposed control algorithm achieves a sublinear convergence rate to the stationary point. Finally, the practical efficacy of HyMoOpt is demonstrated through simulations on a realistic 93-turbine offshore wind farm. Results show that it significantly enhances power output while maintaining strong adaptability under dynamic operational scenarios.

title: Decoupled Controllable-Boundary Model and Coordinated Voltage Support for Renewable Power Plants With Multiple IBRs Under Asymmetric LVRT
Research on Vibration Characteristics of Amorphous Alloy Three-Dimensional Wound Core Transformer Considering Insulating Oil
abstract: Amorphous alloy transformer has energy-saving advantages, but its magnetostrictive effect is higher than that of silicon steel transformer, causing severe vibration and noise, which makes it very easy for amorphous alloy debris to be produced, thereby leading to insulation faults. Additionally, transformer is important power equipment for power delivery. Therefore, in order to reflect the vibration information of the core under different external environments, an analysis model for the transmission of core vibration to the tank is established, to analyze the vibration characteristics of the tank of the amorphous alloy 3D wound core transformer under both insulating oil and non-insulating oil conditions. Firstly, to obtain fundamental magnetization and magnetostriction characteristics, a single-frame amorphous alloy three-dimensional wound (3D) core magnetic property testing platform is constructed. Subsequently, drawing on the principles of elastic mechanics, a magneto-mechanical coupled vibration model is established for amorphous alloy 3D wound core. Meanwhile, a vibration test platform is constructed to obtain the distribution trend of core vibration under different operating conditions, which the accuracy of the finite element model for core vibration is validated. Finally, the investigation is carried on a 50 kVA amorphous alloy wound 3D transformer to evaluate tank’s vibration characteristics under the conditions with and without insulating oil, obtaining vibration intensity and frequency distribution characteristics of the tank, and the accuracy of the tank’s vibration characteristics is validated for transformer model. On this basis, the influence of insulating oil temperature on the tank’s vibration characteristics is considered to reveal the relationship among the vibration characteristics of insulating oil, core, and tank. To break through the limitations of traditional electrical detection methods and provide a theoretical basis for the online fault diagnosis of core.

title: A Full-Cycle Model of the AC Electric Arc Furnace Considering the Production Process
abstract: The existing electric arc furnace models mainly focus on the power quality issues generated during the melting period, failing to fully consider that the smelting process is a continuous and dynamic one. This results in the lack of a complete full-cycle model of the electric arc furnace, thereby restricting the assessment of power quality throughout the entire smelting process. Therefore, this paper proposes a full-cycle model of the AC electric arc furnace considering the production process. Firstly, by analyzing the influence of the production process on the furnace gas during the steelmaking process of the electric arc furnace, the dynamic mapping relationship between the gas concentration changing with time and the microscopic particle behavior in the arc was revealed using the electronic continuity equation. Secondly, based on the magnetic compression force balance equation, the quantitative relationship between pressure and radius was derived, and the function of the arc length change throughout the cycle was constructed. Thirdly, through a combination of mechanism and data, the gas concentration change curves and the arc length change functions for each stage of the smelting process were determined. Finally, using a 55-ton steelmaking AC electric arc furnace as the research object, a model was established on the Matlab/Simulink platform to verify its accuracy. The simulation results show that the proposed model is consistent with the actual production process of the AC electric arc furnace and can accurately reflect the entire power quality cycle of the entire period.

title: Flexible Input/Output Port-Based Energy Router for Integrating Offshore Wind Farms Through Multiform Power Transmission Technologies
abstract: High Voltage Alternating Current (HVAC), Low Frequency Alternating Current (LFAC), and High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) serve as the primary transmission technologies for Offshore Wind Farms (OWFs), typically selected based on specific techno-economic constraints. This technological diversity introduces challenges for the unified grid integration. To facilitate the interconnection of these diverse technologies, an Energy Router for Integrating Offshore Wind Farms (ER-IOWF) with flexible input/output ports is proposed in this paper. The ER-IOWF features a DC bus-centered architecture with dedicated input ports for HVAC, LFAC, and HVDC OWFs, and two output ports for AC and DC grids. A bidirectional converter enables controllable power exchange between the AC and DC grids, supporting multi-path power flow. Furthermore, a hierarchical control strategy is developed to coordinate operational modes and execute port-level regulation, wherein the upper layer manages power allocation via mode coordination and the lower layer implements dual-loop control to track references. Simulation results from both MATLAB/Simulink and a real-time digital simulator confirm that the proposed ER-IOWF enables unified integration and flexible power routing.

title: Stray Current Mitigation With Reverse Running Rail Current Control Strategy for Virtual-Return-Based DC Traction Power Supply System
abstract: The virtual-return-based DC traction power supply system (VRTPS) has been studied to solve the stray current and rail potential issues in urban rail transit. By utilizing the power electronic devices (PEDs) and return line, VRTPS constructs the zero-resistance virtual return path (VRP) by diverting traction current from the running rail into this newly established path. However, the mitigation performance of existing VRTPS control strategies is still suboptimal, leading to incomplete suppression of stray current and rail potential within the train-occupied section. Thus, the reverse running rail current control strategy of VRTPS is proposed to further reduce the stray current and rail potential. Firstly, the topology and modeling of VRTPS are investigated to analyze the inherent limitations of the ideal zero-resistance VRP. Secondly, the detailed analysis of the reverse running rail current control for VRTPS is presented, which optimizes the running rail current distribution with the variable-resistance VRP. Thirdly, the comparative researches on both the stray current and rail potential distribution are conducted between the conventional system and VRTPS with different control strategies. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of VRTPS with proposed strategy on the stray current and rail potential mitigation are validated through simulation and experimental results.

title: Temperature-Based Hybrid Modeling for Heating Power Prediction and Fault Detection in Power Transformers
abstract: Accurate estimation of internal heating power is essential for transformer thermal assessment and fault diagnosis. However, the multi-physics coupling and nonlinear heat transfer in oil-immersed transformers make it difficult to infer heating power directly from external temperatures using purely physical models. This paper proposes a hybrid temperature-based framework that integrates physical understanding with data-driven learning. The physical thermal–electrical model is used to reveal the nonlinear temperature–power relationships, guiding feature selection via mutual information (MI) analysis. Selected temperature features are then applied to a random forest (RF) regressor for heating power prediction. Experiments on a thermally equivalent scaled prototype of a 500 kV power transformer, involving 28 operating cases under both normal and fault conditions, demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high prediction accuracy, with an average test $R^{2}$ of 0.9956 and a test mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 2.27%. Moreover, deviations in predicted heating power under constant load effectively indicate localized thermal anomalies. The results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid approach offers a practical and interpretable solution for transformer condition monitoring using only external temperature measurements.

title: IGBT Open-Circuit Fault Detection and Localization Method for Cascaded H-Bridge Stage of Power Electronic Transformer
abstract: The rectifier stage of power electronic transformers (PETs) commonly employs either a cascaded H-bridge (CHB) or a modular multilevel converter (MMC) topology. Due to its high modularity, scalability, and ease of redundancy design, the CHB topology is widely adopted in PETs. However, the use of numerous power electronic devices in PETs increases the probability of faults. In this paper, a novel fault detection and localization method is proposed for the rapid identification of IGBT open-circuit faults in the CHB stages of PETs. A mathematical model of the CHB grid-side voltage is established, which contains abundant harmonic information. The harmonic characteristics of the grid-side voltage under different IGBT open-circuit faults are analyzed, revealing that the amplitude and phase of even-order carrier frequency harmonics depend on the location of the faulty H-bridges. Based on this characteristic, the fault region is identified. By adjusting the modulation scheme of specific H-bridges and analyzing the resulting variations in the grid-side voltage, multiple IGBT open-circuit faults can be accurately localized. The proposed method utilizes the characteristic harmonics of the H-bridge port theoretical voltage as a reference, thereby reducing fault-identification time and remaining unaffected by load conditions. Its effectiveness is validated through PSCAD/EMTDC simulations and hardware-in-the-loop experiments.

title: Downscaling Method for Ground Flash Density in Transmission Line Corridors Considering Terrain Effects
abstract: Ground Flash Density (GFD) serves as a critical parameter for evaluating the lightning strike risk of transmission lines. It is typically derived from the statistical analysis of data monitored by Lightning Location Systems. However, constrained by the limited sample size of ground flashes and the detection accuracy of Lightning Location Systems, the spatial resolution of GFD is relatively low. To enhance the spatial resolution of GFD along transmission line corridors, this paper proposes a downscaling method of GFD based on the Monte Carlo method considering micro-terrain conditions. For a given original grid area, considering the influence of terrain on lightning, the lightning strike point is determined by the lightning leader fractal model, thereby generating a simulated dataset of ground flash samples dataset. The original grid is further divided into multiple subunits, and the GFD of subunit is calculated by combining the grid average ground flash density statistics, ultimately yielding the high spatial resolution ground flash density. The proposed method is used to calculate GFD in the actual grid area and the effectiveness of the method is verified.

title: A Novel Transient Disturbance Waveform Compression Method in Distribution Networks Based on Dictionary Learning
abstract: The distribution network with a large-scale integration of distributed renewable energy sources exhibits more complex dynamic behavior. The widespread deployment of high-resolution waveform monitoring in distribution networks is hindered by the massive data transmission and storage requirements. To mitigate this communication bottleneck, this paper proposes a novel transient disturbance waveform compression method in distribution networks based on dictionary learning. A new framework for disturbance waveform compression on terminal side and reconstruction on master station side has been proposed to outline the offline learning and online decomposition steps. Then a determination method of the start and end times of transient disturbance waveforms based on the relative energy acceleration operator (REAO) has been proposed for disturbance waveform segmentation, which clarifies the disturbance processes that need to be monitored. To improve the decomposition and reconstruction efficiency, an overcomplete dictionary design method that considers feature redundancy within the dictionary based on clustering pruning optimized K-SVD (CPK-SVD) has been proposed. The redundant atoms in the dictionary are pruned based on Gaussian mixture model (GMM) clustering method after feature extraction. Simulation and field recorded waveform data tests show that the proposed method can achieve a compression ratio of over 10 while ensuring measurement accuracy.

title: Joint Type Diagnosis and Severity Assessment of Partial Discharge in Gas-Insulated Switchgear via Multi-Task Learning
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) is a key indicator of insulation health in gas-insulated switchgear (GIS). It is widely used for condition monitoring in high-voltage power systems. However, the diverse intensities and underlying fault mechanisms of PD often result in complex and variable signal patterns. Traditional single-task learning approaches struggle to capture this complexity and generalize across multiple diagnostic objectives. To address these challenges, we propose PD-MTNet, a multi-task learning framework for simultaneous PD type diagnosis and severity assessment. The framework adopts an attention-enhanced lightweight backbone to extract robust shared representations, tailored to the multi-scale and sparse nature of PRPD data. By highlighting salient discharge regions and suppressing background responses, the backbone effectively captures physically meaningful features across phase–amplitude scales. A multi-path hybrid module is then employed to decouple task-specific features according to their diagnostic mechanisms, facilitating more discriminative representations for each task. This design, together with the shared feature learning strategy, enhances intra-class compactness and inter-class separability. This design improves robustness to ambiguous boundaries and noisy labels, resulting in more stable and physically consistent diagnostic performance. Experimental results demonstrate that PD-MTNet achieves classification accuracies of 97.92% for PD type diagnosis and 95.19% for severity assessment, validating its effectiveness and generalization capability in complex PD diagnostic scenarios.

title: Single-Terminal Fault Location for Multiterminal HVDCs With Branched Topology
abstract: Research on single-terminal fault locations for multiterminal high-voltage direct current (HVDC) with branched topologies remains limited because i) wave propagation is complicated by impedance discontinuities and line-terminal configurations, hindering universal pattern extraction; and ii) conventional Bergeron method introduces substantial errors for long-distance HVDCs, rendering it unsuitable for single-terminal fault location. To address this, an enhanced Bergeron model (EBM) is first proposed. Frequency-specific propagation delays and losses are incorporated through the Laplace transform and computational circuit inversion. Then, the time-reassigned multi-synchrosqueezing transform (TMSST) processes the guessed wave-process (GWP) and actual wave-process (AWP), reconstructing multi-frequency current waves to label wavefront groups. Reconstructed traveling waves are integrated via weighted least squares (WLS) for robustness. Finally, single-terminal fault location is achieved by optimizing fault distance and fault resistance variables to minimize errors between GWP and AWP. Accurate single-terminal fault location is confirmed in Kunliulong three-terminal HVDC. Without using potential transformers, the method requires only a 2-ms time window and operates reliably under strong noise interferences (with a signal-to-noise ratio as low as 25 dB). Without random forest (RF) correction, non-dead-zone faults show 0.74%-2.81% errors, while dead-zone faults maintain practical applicability with ≤4.22% error. After RF incorporation, the error stays below 0.2% regardless of fault locations.

title: Novel Bushing With Adaptively Field Grading Structure: Simulation and Mechanism
abstract: Bushing has become a critical component endangering the safe functioning of power transmission and limiting its development to higher voltage and power levels. The main technical bottleneck that restricts high voltage bushing is the uneven distribution of electric fields due to its “plug-in” structure. In this paper, a novel adaptive field grading (AFG) bushing with a simple multi-layered structure based on nonlinear materials is introduced. A frequency-domain steady-state simulation method considering the field-dependent dielectric and loss characteristics of nonlinear materials to design the AFG bushing is proposed. Referring to the size of the AC transformer capacitive bushing, the finite element models of the 40.5 kV AFG bushing are established, and the electric field distributions are obtained. Optical electric field sensors are used to test the surface electric field distribution of the bushing samples, validating the accuracy of the simulation method. Combining simulation and experimental test results, the influence of doping concentrations and lengths of the field grading layer on the electric field distribution is studied, and the grading mechanism of nonlinear material is summarized. The results demonstrate the potential of nonlinear materials to relieve electric field concentration in bushings and provide a solid basis for its design and application.

title: A Segmented Insulation Assessment Method of Power Cable Based on EWV Inversion
abstract: Compared with the traditional holistic insulation assessment (HIA) methods, which can only provide the insulation condition information of whole cables, segmented insulation assessment (SIA) can provide the insulation condition information of each cable segment, thereby enhancing cable maintenance efficiency. In the past, SIA was achieved by estimating the attenuation coefficient through quantitatively calculating reflected wave amplitudes. However, multiple signal reflections within the cable cause cross-coupling among reflected wave amplitudes, leading to poor generalizability and inaccuracy in SIA. In this article, an SIA method based on velocity inversion using compressive subspace multiple signal classification (CS-MUSIC) is proposed to avoid the problem of the past method. The idea of the proposed method is that electromagnetic wave velocity (EWV) in a power cable is associated with the insulation condition of the cable. The more serious the cable insulation aging, the slower the EWV. Besides, a power cable can naturally be divided into several segments by power cable joints. Consequently, if the EWV in each cable segment can be assessed, the EWV can be used to evaluate the insulation condition of each cable segment. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through simulation, experiment, and a 10kV power cable field test.

title: Investigation of Metal Particles Behavior in the Interruption of Vacuum Switches
abstract: Late breakdown (LB) following interruption has become a critical limitation to the interruption performance of high-voltage (HV) vacuum interrupters (VIs), with metal particles widely considered as a primary key factor. To investigate the particle behavior in-depth during the interruption process, an optical diagnostic platform was developed to observe the metal particles throughout the entire interruption including arcing and post-arc stages. The particle formation under various electrode erosion modes were comprehensively investigated, and their post-arc motion was analyzed through trajectory tracking. Results show that for axial magnetic field (AMF) electrodes, moderately large currents below the rated short-circuit level can trigger intense cathodic activity, leading to abundant metal particles emission from the molten cathode surface, while the anode remains passive. After the current zero (CZ), once emitted particles collide with the contact surface, the cathode spot particles tend to rebound within the gap or off the chamber wall, while molten pool particles are often reabsorbed by the molten electrode surface. Both types of particles can persist in the gap long after CZ. The combined influence of these cathode particles may act as a primary trigger for LB. This study establishes the correlation between interrupting current, cathode activity, and metal particle generation, along with a detailed characterization of their spatiotemporal behavior during the entire interruption.

title: Task-Difficulty-Guided Multi-Gate Mixture-of-Experts for Robust Uncertainty Quantification in Solar Power Forecasting
abstract: Reliable solar power interval forecasting, critical for grid integration and operational planning, is challenged by quantile heterogeneity and non-Gaussian error distributions. This paper introduces a task-difficulty-guided multi-gate mixture-of-experts (TD-M2oE) framework within paired-quantile multi-task learning. TD-M2oE is characterized by a novel masking gate that adaptively allocates experts across varied quantile tasks, yielding coherent prediction intervals across multiple coverage levels. A composite loss enforces quantile monotonicity and promotes expert diversity, empirically enhancing robustness under non-Gaussian and heteroscedastic conditions. Experiments on real-world solar power datasets demonstrate consistent improvements in interval reliability and sharpness over state-of-the-art baselines.

title: A Novel Eigenvalue Structure for Two-Mode Resonance Stability Analysis: SSCIs Between Wind Generation and Power Systems as Examples
abstract: Intensified interactions among diversified devices, especially those for wind generation, have caused many events of subsynchronous control interactions (SSCIs) and posed a challenge to power system stability. It is hard for the classical modal analysis to quantify the interaction among oscillation modes explicitly and explain why the interaction or resonance occurs, because eigenvalues and eigenvectors are not differentiable at the resonance point and move drastically nearby. This paper proposes a novel inherence-interaction eigenvalue structure that manages to extend classical single-mode analysis to two-mode resonance stability and SSCI analysis. In the proposed structure, slow-varying inherent eigenvalues denoting properties of two modes themselves and quantities reflecting their interaction are detached. Hence, the SSCI instability mechanism can be ascribed to and explicitly quantified by damping exchange between two modes under interaction. Variation of the oscillation frequency and eigenvectors can be explained likewise. The proposed theory is used to explain SSCI mechanism between wind generation and power systems, and accurately predict rapidly-changing eigenvalues as well as construct the SSCI stability region under parameter variation. The effectiveness is validated by results on two typical systems and the New England 39-bus system, compared with several existing methods.

title: Structural Design and Performance Optimization of Flexible Connection Structure of On-Load Tap Changer Under Transient Electro-Thermo-Mechanical Coupling
abstract: On-load tap changers (OLTCs) rely on flexible connection structures (FCSs) to maintain conductive circuits between moveable contacts. Stress concentration represents a primary cause of FCS mechanical failure, yet its behavior under transient electro-thermo-mechanical coupling conditions remains insufficiently addressed. This study develops a shape optimization method based on parametric curves and adaptive optimization to mitigate stress concentration in FCSs. Transient coupling stress analyses are performed for both fixed and moveable FCS types, and geometry-specific parametric curves are constructed according to the identified stress concentration locations and their underlying causes. Adaptive parameter optimization yields significant stress reductions in both cases. The analysis is further extended to multiple consecutive switching cycles, providing a more realistic assessment of FCS stress evolution under actual OLTC service conditions.

title: Prediction Method for Audible Noise of High-Altitude Extra-High Voltage AC Transmission Lines Based on Long-Term Observations
abstract: Audible noise (AN) is a critical parameter in the economic and environmental design of extra-high voltage (EHV) AC transmission lines, especially in high-altitude regions. Although several altitude correction factors and AN prediction methods have been proposed based on corona cage tests and long-term observations, the accuracy remains uncertain owing to the limited measurement data from high-altitude transmission lines. This study addresses this gap through long-term observations of four EHV transmission lines on the Tibetan Plateau, combined with existing corona cage test results. The cumulative distribution of AN in rainy weather was obtained from various observation stations. By comparing measured values from stations at different altitudes and combining the experimental results from a movable corona cage, an altitude correction method for AN was developed. Subsequently, by comparing statistical data from four high-altitude observation stations with predicted results from different approaches, the predicted values were found to be overestimated. An improved prediction method for AN in rainy weather was proposed. Additionally, based on the statistical differences observed over one year at multiple long-term observation stations, a method for evaluating AN under varying weather conditions was investigated. A predictive model for AN under different rainfall conditions was developed based on correlation and multiple regression analyses, and its accuracy was validated. The findings of this study provide a crucial reference for the prediction and evaluation of AN from EHV AC transmission lines in high-altitude regions.

title: Autonomous Optimal Control for Wind Farm Integrated MMC-HVDC System Under Sending-End Single-Phase to Ground Fault
abstract: The integration of large-scale wind farm (WF) with modular multilevel converter-based high-voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) systems is promising. However, this integration is challenged by the single-phase-to-ground (SLG) fault at sending-end overhead transmission lines. Existing SLG fault ride-through (FRT) strategies mainly focus on the fault stresses suppression and transient stability improvement. Less attention is paid to the grid voltage unbalance issue and the limited power transfer capability during SLG FRT. To address these issues, this paper proposes an autonomous optimal control (AOC) to enhance the SLG FRT performance. Firstly, considering the long-distance communication delays, autonomous optimization models are respectively established for MMC and WF, where MMC targets to maximize the power transmission while the WF aims to minimize the grid voltage unbalance. Secondly, with semi-definite relaxation (SDR) and second-order cone relaxation (SOCR), the original nonlinear nonconvex optimization models are transformed into computationally tractable convex formulations. Finally, the autonomous optimization models of MMC and WF are independently solved merely based on local measurements, the solutions of which are taken as the control reference during SLG FRT. Compared with the existing SLG FRT control, the proposed AOC can guarantee the maximum transmission of active power for MMC and minimum grid voltage unbalance for WF. Experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed AOC.

title: Micron Particle-Group Motion and Discharge on a Horizontal Insulating Tube in Clean-Air GIS Under Oscillating Impulses
abstract: Clean-air gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) is gaining increasing attention; however, the motion and discharge mechanisms of metal particle groups in the horizontal electric field within the mechanism housing under impulse voltage in air remain poorly understood. To address this, a scaled experimental platform driven by a positive-polarity oscillating impulse voltage is constructed to examine the motion and discharge behaviors of micron-scale metal particle groups of two sizes (500 μm and 50 μm) distributed on the surface of a horizontal insulating tube. The results indicate that particle motion under impulse voltage is probabilistic: 500 μm particles primarily exhibit in-place torsion and horizontal rolling, while 50 μm particles predominantly undergo diffusion and adhesion. Particles of both sizes exhibit four discharge morphologies, namely isolated luminous spots, semi-bridging discharge, two-segment discharge, and surface flashover. At higher voltages, 500 μm particles tend to form two-segment discharges, whereas 50 μm particles are more likely to produce isolated luminous-spot discharges, implying distinct pre-flashover pathways in which dispersed dust promotes distributed multi-spot bridging while coarse particles favor localized streamer initiation via stronger electron supply. The impulse voltage facilitates initial streamer inception and enhances the photoionization process. The resulting burst of force increases the likelihood of particles overcoming resistance and accelerating disintegration, which at that stage suppresses further discharge development. This study provides theoretical support for elucidating the potential hazards posed by metal particles within the mechanism housing of clean-air GIS.

title: Reduced-Scale Test Method for Dynamic Responses of Bundle Conductor Line Following Ice-Shedding
abstract: A reduced-scale test method for dynamic responses of bundle conductor line following ice-shedding is proposed. In this method, hollow cylindrical electromagnets are used to absorb and release mass blocks modelling ice on and ice-shedding from sub-conductors, multiple cameras are utilized to capture the vertical, transverse and torsional vibrations, tension sensors to measure tensions in all sub-conductors, and three-component force sensors to measure the reaction force at hanging points. Without simplifying the bundle conductor line into a single one which was employed in previous works, the proposed reduced-scale model can satisfy the similarities of bending and torsion stiffness at the same time, model the torsional vibration induced by ice-shedding from sub-conductors, and record tension in each sub-conductor. Reduced-scale test platform for a twin-bundle conductor line was established and utilized to study the dynamic characteristics of the twin-bundle conductor line following partial, unzipping and asynchronous ice-shedding from sub-conductors. The method can be extended to investigate dynamic characteristics of bundle conductor lines following any pattern of ice-shedding.

title: Field-Validated Accelerometer-Based Tension Estimation for Overhead Distribution Lines
abstract: This paper presents a proof-of-concept framework validated using field data that estimates the mechanical tension and corresponding sag of overhead distribution conductors using on-conductor accelerometers and a Random Forest (RF) model. One minute-resolution datasets were collected over a one-month period from three 30-m spans of a 22.9-kV-class distribution line test facility at the KEPCO Gochang Test Center under non-energized conditions. The direct sensor output channels (AccX, AccY, AccZ, Roll, and Yaw), together with temperature and wind variables, are used as inputs to the RF regressor. Across the three spans under the tested conditions, the RF model achieves the lowest normalized root mean square error and the highest coefficient of determination, with NRMSE in the range of 0.007–0.012 and R2 values approaching unity for tension estimation. Sag is then computed from the estimated tension using a standard parabolic approximation consistent with IEEE Std 524. The resulting sag traces closely match those obtained from measured tension, with R2 between 0.996 and 0.999 and mean sag errors in the few-millimeter range, well within the installation tolerances prescribed by IEEE Std 524. A rolling 5-fold cross-validation analysis shows small fold-to-fold dispersion within the available dataset, supporting the feasibility of the proposed framework as a proof-of-concept under the tested conditions. The proposed framework therefore demonstrates the feasibility of using accelerometer signals for tension and sag estimation and suggests potential applicability to clearance assessment and condition monitoring under similar operating conditions.

title: Hierarchical Multi-Terminal DC System for Large-Scale Renewable Integration: Topology and Coordinated Control
abstract: As DC power projects transition toward phased construction and higher voltage levels, interconnecting existing systems to form a multi-voltage-level DC grid is a pragmatic choice that balances the wide-area integration of large-scale renewable energy with the maximization of legacy asset utilization. While DC/DC transformer (DCT) topologies provide viable technical paths, scaling them to ultra-high-voltage applications involves considerations such as full-scale hardware requirements and isolation transformer design. To facilitate more flexible phased expansion, this paper proposes a Hierarchical Multi-Terminal DC (HMTDC) system with Coordinated Primary and Secondary Control (CPSC). The topology employs Multi-Voltage-Level Interconnecting MMCs (MVLI-MMCs) rated for the inter-system voltage differential rather than full terminal voltage, enabling gigawatt-level power exchange through significantly reduced converter capacity. The CPSC combines distributed droop-based primary control for rapid disturbance rejection with secondary optimization that coordinates power margins and voltage quality across subsystems. Comprehensive time-domain simulations demonstrate that the proposed framework not only optimizes cross-level power flows but also ensures fault ride-through and rapid recovery under severe AC/DC contingencies, thereby providing a techno-economically viable pathway for evolving multi-voltage-level DC grids.

title: Generalized Circuit Modeling Method of the Low-Frequency Dynamics for Multi-Terminal AC/DC Hybrid System
abstract: A generalized circuit modeling method is proposed to investigate the low-frequency oscillation problem of the AC/DC hybrid system. Firstly, Based on analogy method, the conversion from control block diagram model to circuit model is realized, and the single-port circuit model of photovoltaic-voltage source converter (PV-VSC) is established.
